articles.title: Being raised by NYC first responders gave Bills assistant coach Dean Marlowe a unique 9/11 perspective: 'It affected all of us that day'
articles.summary: Something will trigger a memory of the trauma, but Marlowe said the more time passes, the more it becomes a badge of honor for him and his family.
articles.body:
For most 9-year olds, the sight of a parent picking them up a little more than an hour into the school day might be a welcome one. But 25 years ago, Dean Marlowe realized quickly that something was very wrong.

"I was in the middle of class, and my stepdad came and picked me up from class," Marlowe told Yahoo Sports by phone recently. "I was kind of confused because I was like, 'Hey, what's going on?' I had just gotten to school. And all I remember him saying is that something bad happened in New York City where me and your mom are working, and we have to go there immediately."

That was the morning of 9/11, and Marlowe was just starting to realize how life-changing that day would be.

Mike Neil, Marlowe's stepfather and a police sergeant with the 75th precinct, had worked a late shift the night before as a favor to a friend. Neil had been asleep only a few hours when another officer from the precinct called to summon him back to work. It wasn't until Neil turned on his TV, seeing the second plane hit the World Trade Center, before he understood why.

Neil called his wife, Lisa, a police officer in Harlem's 32nd precinct, who told him to pick up Dean and his older sister, who worked at a bank close to Marlowe's school. Neither parent was sure when they'd see their kids again, knowing that people were dying and the city they were tasked with protecting was being cloaked in fire, smoke and debris.

Most of Marlowe's family — both parents, plus his aunt, cousins, great uncle and granddad — were police officers and firefighters at the time. Some still are in active duty. It was the world Marlowe grew up in. And it was the darkest day in any of their lives.

Neil tried as best he could to explain to Marlowe what was happening and why he needed to go back to work. As he arrived home to Queens, the nightmare sank in for the young boy.

"I was in Queens, and from my house you could still see some of the smoke that was just piling up in the air after that afternoon, that night, that evening-ish," Marlowe said. "You could see smoke everywhere, even miles away.

"My mom and stepdad were there probably for like five or six days, just trying to help clean up — cleaning up bodies, finding body parts. It was so tragic."

But Marlowe also believes it was an event that created a unique bond between the family.

"It was definitely a true tragic moment for our family," he said, "but also a moment for our family to come together and persevere and take this as a united-we-stand moment."

Marlowe is now 34 years old. He spent eight years forging an NFL career, bouncing between five teams but finding a special place to land in Buffalo. Marlowe spent parts of four seasons there, plus one year on the Bills' practice squad, carving out a reputation as a dirty-work specialist, both as a special teamer and part-time safety, becoming a fan and teammate favorite in the process.

"Deano is great," Bills general manager Brandon Beane said. "Super positive. He was a tough player for us in both Carolina and Buffalo."

Marlowe's signature moment in a Bills uniform was an interception against the Miami Dolphins in the 2022 season's wild-card round, taking over the starting role for Damar Hamlin after his cardiac arrest two weeks earlier in Cincinnati. The pick helped vault the Bills' 34-31 victory.

Marlowe retired following the 2024 season, wanting to shift his career to coaching.

"I want to be able to use my leadership and passion to help the next generation of football players reach their highest potential on and off the field," he wrote on X.

Not surprisingly, Marlowe ended up back in Buffalo. First, he had to endure an incredibly trying season as a defensive quality control coach for Oklahoma State in 2025, which ended with the Cowboys at 1-11 — one win followed by 11 straight losses. It was a stark reminder of how tough the game can be at times, but it didn't deter Marlowe from continuing his coaching pursuit.

"You know, it was one of the best worst experiences I've had in my life in terms of football," Marlowe said. "It was a huge learning lesson, and I'm grateful to have that opportunity."

The Bills extended Marlowe an invitation with a Bill Walsh Diversity Coaching Fellowship this summer. The position was temporary, but when his term was up, the team kept Marlowe on staff for the remainder of the season. Whatever the Bills need, Marlowe said, he's willing to help.

"Just being on the field with the guys, game planning, managing as a coach, just all that stuff is … it just feels like I'm back doing what I love. … You know, I just love it, dude," he said. "Even though you know you're not physically out there performing, you're still doing everything more from a mental standpoint, which is great. So I'm having a blast with it."

Marlowe's NFL coaching debut will come Sunday in Houston, in one of the NFL's biggest Week 1 matchups: Bills at Texans, two teams talented enough to meet again in the playoffs. It will be a special moment in his new career. But coming two days after the 25th anniversary of 9/11, with tributes planned for every game , there also will be other emotions running through his mind.

"It hits a little bit different because my family ties that I have to it are just to the point where it feels like that day my whole family was affected — physically, yes, but also mentally and emotionally," Marlowe said.

How 9/11 has changed Marlowe's perspective

Every year, as 9/11 approaches, Marlowe can't help but look back on that day. It's a story he's told before, notably to the Detroit Free Press during his time as a Lion . This time 25 years have passed, and he's now a full-grown man with a family of his own, embarking on a career shift. Something will trigger a memory of the trauma, but Marlowe said the more time passes, the more it becomes a badge of honor for him and his family.

"It means something to me when I ever see a reminder, a commercial, a post, or anything about 9/11. I kind of get chills," Marlowe said. "It's not a negative emotion, though. It's more of a proud feeling, because almost my whole family — everyone was involved.

"It affected all of us that day, and it still does."

Not everyone in the family is able to see 9/11 in as inspiring a way as Marlowe does. His great uncle, Peter O'Donohue, was part of the FDNY's special operations command on Roosevelt Island in 2001. On the morning of the attacks — O'Donohue's wedding anniversary — he got off work around 7 a.m. and had breakfast with some of his fellow firemen. It was the last time they were all together.

O'Donohue had the day off and went home, planning to celebrate that night with his wife. The rest of his crew got ready for work. None of them made it home that night. All 10 were in the WTC towers when they collapsed.

"He actually lost his entire ladder that day. He survived," Marlowe said. "He woke up a few hours later and … he was like, 'Holy moly, that should have been me with my ladder that had passed.'

"He doesn't like to talk about it often. He still lives with survivor's guilt. He acknowledges such a horrific but proud moment for the country. But he just doesn't go into detail about it because he still suffers from some really traumatic stuff."

Marlowe has a large tattoo running down his leg, which he refers to as his 9/11 memorial, honoring his first-responder family members, including his second cousin, Donald Burns, a deputy fire chief who died just minutes after helping set up a command center in the South Tower before it came crashing down.

"I have my mom and stepdad's badge number. I have my great uncle's badge number, my second cousin's badge number as well," Marlowe said. "So yeah, it means a lot every time I see it."

Marlowe might not have followed his family direction into becoming a first responder, and he's not sure if 9/11 had a way of pushing him more toward football or not. He also knows that comparing the adversity he's faced as a player and coach, being cut multiple times and enduring a 1-11 season his first year coaching, isn't at all tantamount to the tragedy he and his family endured 25 years ago.

But Marlowe has always tried to find strength in darker times, using his family's strength as his north star.

"The one thing I always think is that when there's something bad that happens in life, anyone can learn from it. The crazy thing — and I hate to say it like this — is that the sun rises the next day. Not to disregard things that happened, but if you know that at the end of the day the sun is gonna come back up the next day … that's life."

"It showed the resilience of my family and showed the resilience of the country. The amount of endless hours that my family members were working, and the strength it took to really go out there and help our country.

"It takes a village for everything. I live my life like that when I'm in sports and in my regular life with my family. No one can ever be truly successful by themselves. You're never in it alone."

With every year that passes, and every milestone 9/11 that arrives, Marlowe realizes just how much that one day has helped shape his life.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $300,000 cancer donation and $80 million orphanage claim sparked heavy controversy
articles.summary: NFL News: A new viral story involving Travis Kelce has been exposed as false, after social media posts claimed the Kansas City Chiefs star and his fiancée had s.
articles.body: A new viral story involving Travis Kelce has been exposed as false, after social media posts claimed the Kansas City Chiefs star and his fiancée had spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on a child battling brain cancer. The same posts also tied Kelce to an alleged $80 million orphanage project. However, no credible evidence supports either claim, with the story appearing to be another example of AI-generated celebrity misinformation.Travis Kelce donation rumor fails to hold upThe claim began circulating on Facebook in late November, packaged as a dramatic breaking-news story about Kelce and his charitable efforts. Posts alleged that the NFL tight end and his fiancée had paid $300,000 toward medical treatment for a 2-year-old child with brain cancer.The story then went much further. It claimed the couple planned to spend $80 million building what was described as the largest free orphanage in the United States.For Kelce, the rumor is notable because it follows a growing pattern of fabricated stories that attach his name to emotional charity cases. The posts used images designed to make the claims look convincing, including pictures of Kelce and his fiancée alongside a hospitalized toddler and a building carrying a sign that read "Taylor Swift Orphanage."A closer look, however, found no credible news reports confirming the alleged $300,000 donation or the orphanage plan. The websites spreading the claim also appeared to be designed to attract clicks and advertising revenue.That matters because the story was not simply an unverified social media post. It was presented with the tone and appearance of a major charitable announcement, encouraging readers to accept an extraordinary claim before checking its source.Travis Kelce has previously warned about AI charity storiesThe latest rumor also fits with an issue Kelce has addressed before. In April 2025, he responded on his "New Heights with Jason & Travis Kelce" podcast to another false claim about his charitable activities.While discussing the spread of fabricated stories, Kelce said, "This time I wasn't doing what was falsely claimed by the social channels or the outlets posting all this AI stuff."He also pointed audiences toward 87running.org, the website for his foundation, as a place to find authentic information about his charitable work.There is an important distinction behind the latest rumor. A real story reported in October 2025 said that his fiancée donated $100,000 to help the family of a 2-year-old child battling brain cancer. That genuine act may have provided the seed for the much larger fabricated claim involving Kelce, $300,000 and an $80 million orphanage.Kelce has also been involved in legitimate charitable work, making it easier for false stories to appear believable when they use his name. But the absence of reliable reporting is a major warning sign.The episode is another reminder that emotional celebrity stories can travel quickly online, especially when they involve children, illness and huge donations. For readers, checking the original source and looking for confirmation from established news organizations remains one of the simplest ways to separate genuine philanthropy from an AI-generated viral rumor.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Former NFL star LeShon Johnson sentenced to five years in prison over massive dogfighting ring
articles.summary: NFL News: Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson has been sentenced to five years in federal prison after being convicted in connection with a large-scale dogfi.
articles.body: Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson has been sentenced to five years in federal prison after being convicted in connection with a large-scale dogfighting operation in Oklahoma. The case has drawn renewed attention to his life after football, with prosecutors describing a long-running operation that caused the deaths and serious injuries of hundreds of dogs.LeShon Johnson receives five-year prison sentence in dogfighting caseJohnson, 55, received his sentence Thursday in an Oklahoma federal court. Along with five years behind bars, he was ordered to serve three years of supervised release and pay a $30,000 fine.The former running back surrendered 190 dogs to the government following his conviction. According to the Department of Justice, that was the largest number of dogs seized from a single person in a federal dogfighting case.Federal prosecutors linked Johnson to Mal Kant Kennels, an Oklahoma operation that had been breeding and trafficking pit bulls since at least 2007. Investigators said the dogs were bred for fighting traits and that Johnson promoted bloodlines connected to successful fighting dogs.The case is especially serious because this was not Johnson's first encounter with dogfighting charges. He pleaded guilty to state dogfighting charges in 2004 and received a five-year deferred sentence, according to court records.His latest conviction involved six felony counts tied to possessing, selling, transporting and delivering dogs for use in animal fighting.Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. strongly condemned the operation after the sentence was announced."LeShon Johnson will face justice for building another particularly egregious and violent dog fighting scheme," associate attorney general Stanley E. Woodward Jr. said in a statement Thursday. "As Johnson was well aware, dog fighting is a felony in all 50 states. To anyone attempting to build violent and illicit business schemes: you can run, but you can't hide from the Department of Justice."Former NFL player LeShon Johnson could appeal sentenceJohnson's legal team had pushed for a much lighter punishment. His attorney, Billy Coyle IV, asked the court to consider probation and pointed to Johnson's medical condition, his lack of recent criminal history and the fact that he had remained on pretrial release for more than two years without violations.Coyle also argued that Johnson had serious health problems and had experienced multiple concussions and traumatic brain injuries during his football career. Court documents said he had required a daily caretaker for the past two years."The main point was just to show the court that he'd been out on bond for pretrial release for over two years," Coyle said. "He's got no infractions whatsoever. He doesn't drink. He doesn't smoke. I don't think the necessity of sending him to prison or jail was necessary."Coyle later said he was surprised by the five-year sentence and expected to recommend an appeal, although Johnson had not made a final decision.Prosecutors had sought a 10-year sentence, arguing that Johnson played a leadership role in the operation. They also pointed to the deaths and injuries involving hundreds of dogs as a reason against reducing his punishment.Johnson's football career once put him in the national spotlight. He played for the Green Bay Packers, Arizona Cardinals and New York Giants between 1994 and 1999 before later playing in the XFL. At Northern Illinois, he earned unanimous All-American honors in 1993 and finished sixth in Heisman Trophy voting.His federal sentence now marks a stark and troubling chapter in the former NFL player's post-football life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I don’t care if people are judging": Alix Earle’s breakup with Braxton Berrios takes a shocking turn as Tom Brady becomes part of the drama
articles.summary: NFL News: Alix Earle is giving viewers a closer look at a complicated chapter of her relationship with NFL star Braxton Berrios. The former couple had not offic.
articles.body: Alix Earle is giving viewers a closer look at a complicated chapter of her relationship with NFL star Braxton Berrios. The former couple had not officially split when conversations about their Netflix reality series began, meaning the breakup unfolded while the project was already taking shape. Now, Earle is addressing the timing and explaining why filming captured such an emotional period in her life.Alix Earle and Braxton Berrios breakup timeline takes an unexpected turnWhen Earle and her family first explored making a reality show in summer 2025, she was still in a relationship with Berrios. The idea was not built around a breakup storyline. In fact, Earle initially questioned whether their everyday lives offered enough drama or excitement to keep an audience interested.That uncertainty quickly disappeared.As production moved forward, the relationship entered a difficult period. Their eventual split became one of the defining parts of Earle Meets World, which follows Earle and her family through an unusually turbulent stretch of their lives.The situation also puts the show's emotional scenes in a different light. Rather than entering the project with a breakup already planned, Earle found herself documenting a relationship that was changing in real time.She pushed back against the idea that she deliberately prolonged the breakup because cameras were rolling. Earle explained that her emotions were genuine, even when viewers questioned her decisions.“I’m just a girl and going through a breakup,” she says. “I don’t care if it’s my 45th time crying about it — it’s how I feel. And I just tried to put it out there. I’m like, ‘I don’t care if people are judging me and saying it’s crazy.’ ”Her comments underline one of the show's central tensions. Viewers are not simply watching a polished celebrity romance. They are seeing someone deal with uncertainty, heartbreak and public scrutiny while knowing that millions of people may eventually judge every decision.Braxton Berrios leaves Alix Earle relationship story with a cliffhangerThe breakup itself is not the only moment keeping viewers talking. The finale leaves the door slightly open when Earle contacts Berrios and asks whether he could ever imagine the two of them getting back together.His response is brief, but it carries plenty of weight.“Oh, Alix.”Those two words arrive after an entire season of relationship tension, making the ending deliberately ambiguous. Earle later acknowledged that even she found the scene stressful to watch.Asked whether reconciliation remains possible, she did not completely close the door.“We’re on good terms, and for what the future holds, we don’t know. We will see.”That uncertainty has helped keep interest in the Alix Earle and Braxton Berrios breakup story alive. Their relationship ended, but the reality series shows that emotional endings are rarely as neat as they appear online.All eight episodes of Earle Meets World are now streaming on Netflix, allowing viewers to follow the relationship story from its earlier uncertainty through the breakup and its unresolved final moment.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I’m done": Patrick Mahomes reaches breaking point as knee injury doubts continue to overshadow Chiefs’ Week 1 opener
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is nearing the moment he has been working toward since undergoing knee surgery, but the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback appears to have.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is nearing the moment he has been working toward since undergoing knee surgery, but the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback appears to have little patience left for questions about his recovery. With the season opener against the Denver Broncos approaching, Mahomes made his feelings clear while addressing reporters, as attention turns from his rehabilitation to his return under center.Patrick Mahomes Sets Clear Boundary On Knee Injury QuestionsMahomes’ frustration surfaced during his Thursday media session when another question about his physical condition brought a blunt response. Rather than provide another detailed update, the three-time Super Bowl winner signaled that he wants the conversation to move forward.“Hopefully I’m done with the questions about the leg,” he told reporters.It is an understandable stance for a player who has spent months focused on getting back on the field. Mahomes suffered ACL and LCL tears in his left knee during the Chiefs’ December meeting with the Los Angeles Chargers. The injury immediately created uncertainty around his availability for the opening weeks of the 2026 NFL season.Yet Mahomes never appeared willing to let the injury change his target. He identified Week 1 as the goal from the outset and built his rehabilitation around reaching that date.The quarterback explained in August that his doctors had initially estimated a nine-month recovery if everything progressed properly.“It’s nine months. It’s the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week One. I’m someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right. This has always been the plan. From the day I got the surgery, as quick as I did, to hopefully the first game of the year, the plan will go accordingly, and I’ll be able to go out there and be myself.”Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes Expected To Start Against BroncosThe most important development for Kansas City came from head coach Andy Reid. His comments offered the clearest indication yet that Mahomes could be under center when the Chiefs begin their campaign against Denver.Reid stopped short of making an absolute guarantee, leaving room for something unexpected to change during the final days before kickoff. Still, his assessment was strongly positive.“As far as our roster goes, there's a very good chance that Patrick will go ahead and start unless something were to come up here in the next couple days,” Reid told reporters. “Most likely he'll be the guy that's out there.”For the Chiefs, Mahomes’ return carries significance beyond simply having their starting quarterback available. His ability to move comfortably, handle pressure and regain his usual rhythm will be closely watched once the competitive action begins.The opening game should provide the first meaningful test of how far his recovery has come. Until then, Mahomes appears determined to let his preparation speak louder than repeated injury updates.The Chiefs now have a straightforward objective: get their franchise quarterback through the final stretch of preparation and into Week 1 ready to play.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Seahawks fan chat: Who do you want to see lose more, the Rams or 49ers?

articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks started their 2026 season with a comeback win over the New England Patriots , ensuring that they'll be ahead of at least one of the San Francisco 49ers or Los Angeles Rams by the end of Week 1. Seattle and New England had to play on Wednesday to accommodate the Niners and Rams debuting regular season NFL in Australia. What is technically a Thursday night game in the United States is a Friday morning kickoff in Melbourne, and we'll soon find out if staying in Australia for a week is a better strategy than flying in about as late as reasonably possible like the Rams did.

While unfortunately both of these teams cannot start the season 0-1, we'll either see one of them at 0-1 by the end of tonight or 0-0-1 in the unlikely event of a tie. Consider that the 49ers play the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals the next two weeks and they could start the season 3-0, two weeks out before they face the Seahawks. Meanwhile, the Rams still have the Denver Broncos , Philadelphia Eagles , and Buffalo Bills to come over the next few weeks, so it's not like they have an easy schedule. It's a division game, so the tiebreakers will be very important for Seahawks fans to watch.

The 49ers are as healthy as can be as far as their star players, while the Rams have everyone except Aaron Donald all good to go.

articles.title: Patriots WR A.J. Brown expected to miss at least 4 weeks with high ankle sprain
articles.summary: An MRI on Thursday confirmed the injury, which Brown sustained during New England's loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots might be without star wide receiver A.J. Brown for longer than they hoped.

An MRI on Thursday reportedly confirmed that Brown suffered a high ankle sprain, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks with the injury, per Rapoport. High ankle sprains typically require four to six weeks of recovery.

Brown suffered the injury during the third quarter of Wednesday night's loss to the Seattle Seahawks , with the 29-year-old receiver grabbing at his lower right leg after an incompletion. Brown stayed down while athletic staff tended to him before he was helped off the field.

Postgame, Brown was reportedly seen leaving the locker room in a walking boot on his right foot. Prior to leaving the game, Brown had three receptions for 26 yards.

Overall, it wasn't the best night for the Patriots, with quarterback Drake Maye throwing a mind-boggling interception to basically end the game, and receiver Romeo Doubs notably failing to grab any of his three targets, including a brutal drop in the second half. The Seahawks rallied to a 13-10 win after scoring 10 points in the fourth quarter.

Given the recovery timeline, it's possible the Patriots will choose to place Brown on injured reserve, which will require him to miss the next four games. New England 's next game isn't until Sept. 20 (as a result of the unusual Wednesday opener), but a four-week absence would land Brown's return somewhere around the Patriots' Week 6 game against the New York Jets .

Brown wasn't the only notable injury in Wednesday's game: Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury very early in the matchup. However, Darnold's outlook appears more optimistic, as the veteran QB avoided a fracture and is instead reportedly dealing with an unusual muscle strain .

The Patriots had acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles as part of a big offseason trade in June, with the hope of reigniting the receiver's talent. Instead, it looks like they'll be without him for the first chunk of the year.

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs Named a Major Winner of Lions Offseason
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs got paid this offseason, and one Lions writer thinks the bigger prize is still coming. #Lions
articles.body:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was rewarded in August with a three-year, $67.5 million contract extension , a deal that made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history as he enters his fourth season. He is one of the core pieces on this offense for the Lions.

Gibbs is primed for a huge season after the Lions traded running back David Montgomery to the Houston Texans in March. As the featured three-down back, it is quite possible that Gibbs can carry the ball more than 300 times in the 2026 NFL season.

Candace Pedraza of Side Lion Report listed five winners and three losers from the offseason as Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season approaches. Gibbs landed on the winners side alongside the rookie class, Aidan Hutchinson , Isaac TeSlaa and the team's undrafted free agents. Pedraza wrote:

"Gibbs has an excellent shot at winning OPOY or MVP, or both, this season. He's not only about to see a major uptick in carries this season with the trade of Montgomery going down this offseason, but the Lions' "light" schedule should make his ability to break some rushing records fairly simple. That's all assuming, of course, that the Lions' offensive line makes his life this easy. But, coming off a historic extension and getting handed the keys to the ground game should be extra motivation for a competitor like Gibbs this season."

articles.title: Cowboys WR, TE Get New Contracts Ahead of NFL Season Opener vs. Giants, Updated Salary Cap
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have reportedly signed tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year, $18 million extension that includes $12 million in guaranteed money, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have reportedly signed tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year, $18 million extension that includes $12 million in guaranteed money, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.

Wideout Ryan Flournoy also signed a one-year, $6 million extension on Thursday night:

According to Spotrac the Cowboys currently have $23.3 million in top-51 cap space for the 2027 season, when Spann-Ford and Flournoy's extensions kick in.

Spann-Ford, 26, has spent the past two seasons with the Cowboys after being an undrafted free agent out of Minnesota, registering 18 catches for 178 yards and a touchdown in 34 games. He's largely served as depth behind Jake Ferguson, who has remained an important target for Dak Prescott.

Ferguson is under contract through the 2029 season, so barring a release for salary-cap purposes, he and Spann-Ford should be the one-two punch for the Cowboys at tight end for many years to come.

Flournoy, 26, has caught 50 passes for 577 yards and four touchdowns in 27 games across the past two seasons in Dallas.

articles.title: “We are beyond thankful for everyone’s support”: How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned Team 62 into a $3.69M legacy for the autism community

articles.body: Jason and Kylie Kelce have turned a summer charity event into something much bigger than a yearly fundraiser. Since Team 62 began in 2021, the event has brought Eagles fans, families and members of the autism community together while creating another major source of support for the Eagles Autism Foundation.The sixth annual Team 62 fundraiser continued that growth in 2026. Held on June 24 in Sea Isle City, the event raised more than $1.26 million in a single night, taking the total raised through the fundraiser since 2021 beyond $3.69 million. What started as a local community event has steadily become one of the most recognizable charitable weekends connected to the Eagles and the Kelce family.How Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned Team 62 into a growing traditionThe success of Team 62 has never depended only on one evening. Jason and Kylie have helped build an entire weekend around the cause, giving people different ways to participate while keeping the focus on the autism community.The 2026 weekend included an all-abilities football clinic, a cheerleading clinic and an Eagles drumline workshop. Families could also take part in beach yoga and other activities in Sea Isle City. The mix of events helped make the weekend more inclusive, allowing people of different abilities and ages to join in rather than making the fundraiser feel like a traditional celebrity charity event.The main fundraiser at Ocean Drive brought together current and former Eagles players, Eagles cheerleaders, mascot SWOOP and members of the Kelce family, including Donna Kelce. Guests could support the cause through tips, raffles, merchandise purchases and other donations.Jason and Kylie later shared their appreciation for everyone who helped make the latest event such a success. “We are beyond thankful for everyone’s support and generosity in setting a Team 62 fundraising record,” they said.The fundraising continued beyond Ocean Drive, too. The fourth annual Beer Bowl at the Sea Isle City Yacht Club, an online auction and entry fees from other community activities all contributed to the weekend's total. Together, those efforts helped the sixth Team 62 fundraiser raise more than $1.26 million. How Team 62 became part of the Kelces’ lasting Eagles legacyJason Kelce’s connection with Philadelphia has always gone beyond what happened on the football field. He spent his entire NFL career with the Eagles, became one of the most recognizable players in franchise history and remained closely connected with the city following his retirement. Team 62 has given him and Kylie another way to maintain that connection while supporting a cause that reaches far beyond football.The Eagles Autism Foundation has also recognized the role the couple has played in growing the fundraiser. Executive Director Ryan Hammond praised Jason and Kylie as outstanding ambassadors for the foundation, pointing to their passion and creative approach as reasons Team 62 has become such an important annual event.For the Kelces, however, the latest record was never presented as their achievement alone. They credited the Eagles organization, Sea Isle City and the supporters who continue to return each year.“Six years later, we now stand here amazed at what we’ve accomplished for the autism community,” Jason and Kylie said. They also gave a special thank-you to the Eagles organization, the town of Sea Isle City and “the best fans in the world” for continuing to support the cause.With more than $3.69 million raised since 2021, Team 62 has clearly grown beyond its beginnings. The $1.26 million night added another major chapter, but the lasting part of the Kelces’ work may be the community they have created around the fundraiser, giving families a welcoming place to come together while supporting the Eagles Autism Foundation year after year.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. If Stribling's injury is a long-term concern, Robinson should be a popular target on waivers this week.

articles.body: Brock Purdy entered the 2022 NFL Draft as the very last pick. No fanfare, no guaranteed roster spot, and no certainty that his professional football career would even last a season. She was a multi-sport athlete at Sumner-Fredericksburg High School, serving as a volleyball team captain twice before graduating in 2018. Track and field was also part of her athletic resume, but volleyball was always her primary focus.She enrolled at Iowa State University to continue playing at the college level, studying kinesiology. That is where she and Purdy first found themselves on the same campus. Purdy arrived at Iowa State around the same time to begin his college football career under center for the Cyclones.Brandt spent three seasons playing volleyball for Iowa State, with her college journey including USA Volleyball tryouts and an international trip to South America. Then in late 2020, she transferred to the University of Northern Iowa, where she completed her collegiate playing career with the Panthers in 2022.How did Brock Purdy and Jenna Brandt meet?Their Iowa State connection is where the story starts, though the couple kept things private for a while. Photos together appeared on social media before they ever made anything official. It was not until November 2022 that Brandt publicly shared images with Purdy alongside family members, giving the clearest signal yet that their relationship had grown into something serious.The timing is worth noting. Purdy had just been selected 262nd overall in that year's draft, the final pick, which earned him the unofficial title of "Mr. Irrelevant." He was still proving himself on the field. Brandt, meanwhile, had quietly been part of his life well before any of that.When did Brock Purdy propose to Jenna Brandt?Purdy proposed in July 2023 in St. Cloud, Florida. Both shared the moment on social media, and Purdy made no effort to hide his excitement about what came next. Less than a year later, on March 9, 2024, they married in Des Moines. Brandt wore a strapless mermaid-style gown for the ceremony.Do Brock Purdy and Jenna Brandt have children?The couple became parents in July 2025 when their daughter, Millie Joleen Purdy, arrived. They announced the birth through a joint post on social media, sharing the first photo of their family of three. articles.title: “When someone has an argument...": How Aaron Rodgers’ friendship with Mina Kimes fell apart after his controversial views changed their friendship
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers has never been shy about speaking his mind, but his appearance on the *Not Just Football with Cam Heyward* podcast on September 10 cross.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has never been shy about speaking his mind, but his appearance on the *Not Just Football with Cam Heyward* podcast on September 10 crossed from opinion into something more personal. The 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback called out NFL analyst Mina Kimes by name, claiming she was among the media friends who turned on him after he spoke out against COVID vaccinations. What followed was a candid, at times sharp, account of how one decision reshaped nearly every professional relationship he had built in the media.What exactly did Aaron Rodgers say about Mina Kimes?Aaron Rodgers made it clear that the fallout was not limited to Kimes alone. He recalled a time when the media genuinely valued his perspective — on Colin Kaepernick, on social issues, even on moments that earned him a handwritten note from President Obama. "Everybody loved hearing my takes," he said. "Mina Kimes had me to her house for a feature I did. All of these people were my friends in the media. Until I came out against COVID."That line carries a lot of weight. Rodgers is not just describing a friendship that faded. He is describing a pattern — a conditional kind of acceptance that disappeared the moment his views became inconvenient.He pushed back on the criticism that followed, arguing that his critics abandoned facts for personal attacks. "When someone has an argument and all they can ever say is, they attack your character instead of the content of what you're actually saying, you know that you're actually on the right side of things," he said.Why did Aaron Rodgers say he used the word "immunized" in 2021?This is where Rodgers gets into territory he has revisited multiple times over the years. He explained that his use of the word "immunized" was tied to an active appeal he was making to the NFL regarding his vaccination status. "When I said I was immunized, it was because that statement alone was the crux of my entire argument and ongoing appeal with the NFL around my vaccination status," he said on the podcast.Rodgers later admitted he had avoided the vaccines due to an allergy to polyethylene glycol and expressed skepticism about the Johnson and Johnson vaccine. His appeal to the NFL, which sought to have treatment from a holistic doctor count toward his vaccination status, was ultimately denied.Beyond the semantics, Rodgers says the bigger issue was how unvaccinated players were treated inside team facilities. "Not to mention the hypocrisy around the treatment of players that were non-vaxxed, the inhumane way that we were treated as secondhand citizens around the facility, the way that we couldn't do anything on the road," he said.How did Mina Kimes respond to Rodgers' comments?Kimes addressed Rodgers' vaccination controversy just two days earlier, on September 8, during an appearance on *The Sports Gossip Show*. "It was interesting to see him rehash the COVID stuff," she said. "He clearly was very bothered by the criticism."Kimes was careful to separate the issue. Her criticism, she said, was never about Rodgers being unvaccinated. "The criticism was that he lied about it by omission or whatever," she explained. She also pointed to Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins, who similarly pushed back against the vaccine but largely avoided the same level of media scrutiny. "I think those two are an interesting point of comparison," she added.That comparison is pointed. It suggests the media's response to Rodgers was not purely about vaccine hesitancy but about the specific way he handled the truth around it.What does this say about Rodgers heading into the 2026 season?Rodgers also called Fauci "an absolute, in my opinion, criminal," adding that people -- especially Black Americans -- should have "a healthy skepticism" toward government health agencies.His comments landed just days before his first game of the 2026 season, with the Steelers set to host the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium. At 42, Rodgers is likely in his final NFL season. And yet, rather than stepping back from controversy, he is leaning into it -- revisiting old grievances with the same conviction that created them in the first place.Whether you agree with him or not, the Rodgers-Kimes story is really a story about how COVID permanently rewired sports media relationships and drew lines that, five years later, have never fully moved.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 49ers vs. Rams Fantasy Takeaways, Outlook for Mike Evans, CMC, Davante Adams, Puka Nacua, More
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams kicked off their seasons in Melbourne on Thursday as the Niners picked up a win against their divisional rival.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams kicked off their seasons in Melbourne on Thursday as the Niners picked up a win against their divisional rival.

The game had more than just divisional race implications, though, as it offered some insight for fantasy football players.

After a telling performance from several players, here's some fantasy outlook on Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, and more stars.

When Mike Evans signed with the 49ers this offseason, some fairly assumed that the 33-year-old would ease into a second option role for San Francisco as he enters the late stages of his career.

Evans shattered those assumptions very quickly.

The veteran hauled in six catches for 49 yards and a touchdown, establishing himself as one of Brock Purdy's favorite targets in their first game together.

If the Evans and Purdy connection continues through the season, he'll be a valuable fantasy asset this year.

While one veteran receiver proved he still has plenty left in the tank, another struggled to dispel the notion that he's declining.

Rams wide receiver Davante Adams, also 33, had just three receptions for 26 yards.

It's hard to judge Adams' outlook for the season after a game where the Rams' offense struggled as much as it did, but it certainly isn't a good sign of what's to come.

He was already a second option to Puka Nacua last year, and it doesn't look like he'll make a big impact in fantasy this year.

49ers running back Christian McCaffrey missed some time during training camp because of what the team described as tightness, and he appeared to be shaking off some rust in Week 1.

McCaffrey finished Thursday's win with 68 rushing yards, 20 receiving yards and no touchdowns. He had 10 carries compared to 14 for Kaelon Black.

It's not uncommon for McCaffrey to have a slow Week 1, though, so fantasy managers shouldn't panic just yet.

Puka Nacua Needs MVP Version of Matthew Stafford

Rams receiver Puka Nacua firmly established himself as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL last year when he recorded 1,715 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns, but that season also came as Matthew Stafford won his first MVP award.

To state the obvious, Nacua goes as Stafford does.

Stafford was far from his 2025 self on Thursday as he had just 155 yards and an interception, completing 15 of his 25 passes. That led to a relatively quiet showing from Nacua, who had five receptions for 74 yards.

Nacua and Stafford are one of the best duos in the NFL when they're clicking, but fantasy managers need them to get on the same page in Week 2.

Rams' Backfield Could Cause Issues for Managers

The Rams have a good problem in the fact that they have two running backs more than capable of putting up big numbers.

But that good problem for the Rams could make things difficult for fantasy managers.

Kyren Williams was likely an easy pick for fantasy managers since he's produced double-digit touchdowns in three consecutive seasons, but Blake Corum is quickly catching up to him in terms of production.

Williams accounted for 41 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, while Corum had 54 yards on 10 carries. Williams saw far more snaps in the first half, though, getting 19 to Corum's seven, according to Nathan Jahnke of Pro Football Focus.

Using the running backs equally as Sean McVay did on Thursday is good for Los Angeles since it can avoid wear and tear on just one player, but it also means Williams and Corum's stock could go down this year.

Williams is still likely the best option of the two, especially since he was more active in the passing game.

articles.title: 49ers Beat Rams, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Garrett, Stafford, Evans, CMC, Purdy, Top Players
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers opened the team's 2026 campaign with a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers opened the team's 2026 campaign with a 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia.

Brock Purdy and the 49ers' offense thrived, while Matthew Stafford and the Rams' offensive unit routinely struggled to finish drives.

The two NFC West rivals faced off in front of a packed crowd at Melbourne Cricket Ground, as 100,021 fans were in attendance.

Neither team got off to a particularly strong start offensively, combining for three punts on four drives in the first quarter. San Francisco held a 3-0 lead heading into the second.

Los Angeles eventually found the end zone first, as Kyren Williams' five-yard rushing touchdown put his team up 7-3.

The Rams appeared to be gaining more momentum after a pass from Purdy was picked off by safety Quentin Lake on San Francisco's ensuing drive, but Stafford immediately followed it up with an interception of his own.

Purdy got back on track quickly, connecting with Demarcus Robinson for a 39-yard touchdown to put the 49ers in front once again.

Both teams traded punts on their next two drives, as San Francisco entered halftime with a 10-7 advantage.

The 49ers' offense stayed hot in the second half, moving deep into Los Angeles' territory to open the third quarter before Mike Evans hauled in a short pass from Purdy in the end zone.

The Rams appeared to be on the verge of responding, driving down to San Francisco's one-yard line on their next possession.

However, the 49ers' defensive front stopped a quarterback sneak by Stafford on fourth down to complete a goal-line stand and give the ball back to their offense.

San Francisco took advantage of the opportunity by going on an 11-play, 99-yard drive that ended with a touchdown pass from Purdy to Deebo Samuel.

As Los Angeles attempted to mount a late comeback, 49ers linebacker Fred Warner forced a fumble from Rams tight end Tyler Higbee for another turnover.

San Francisco eventually cruised to the win, as the Rams were held scoreless over the final two quarters of action.

While it's worth noting that Los Angeles was without future Hall of Famer Aaron Donald during the game, Myles Garrett still had a relatively quiet night.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year, who set a new single-season record with 23 sacks in 2025, wasn't able to bring down Purdy in his Rams debut. Garrett also didn't register a tackle.

San Francisco thrived on the ground throughout the contest, rushing for 174 yards as a team while averaging 5.8 yards per carry. The 49ers picked up 23 first downs compared to just 15 for the Rams as well.

Los Angeles fell to 0-1 with the season-opening defeat as San Francisco moved to 1-0.

articles.body: MELBOURNE, Australia — Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel caught touchdown passes from Brock Purdy, and the San Francisco 49ers routed the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 Friday in the first NFL regular-season game in Australia. Purdy passed for 205 yards against the Rams’ ineffective defense at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of 100,021 fans, the seventh-largest regular-season crowd in NFL history. Australia’s sporting capital reveled in its first real taste of American football — and in a dominant win by the 49ers, who had already won many Aussies’ affection by traveling to Melbourne a week earlier than the Rams, who only boomeranged in on Thursday morning. A party atmosphere prevailed even with a Friday morning kickoff necessary to hit the lucrative primetime television audiences in the U.S. The fans got another memorable chapter in this NFC West rivalry as the 49ers blasted the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams with superior play on both sides of the ball. Kyren Williams scored the NFL’s first Australian touchdown on a 5-yard rush to begin the second quarter, but the Rams were a disaster Down Under. Los Angeles hadn’t lost by more than seven points since November 2024. While Purdy’s offense managed enough big plays to win, the San Francisco defense frustrated NFL MVP Matthew Stafford into a 15-of-25 performance for just 155 yards. The Niners held the NFL’s best offense last season to one score, even stopping Stafford on a fourth-down quarterback sneak from the San Francisco 1 in the third quarter. Reigning AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was practically invisible in his Rams debut after missing much of training camp with aches, recording zero tackles. Much of the pregame talk for this trip centered on the teams’ starkly differing methods of preparation: The 49ers ingratiated themselves with the local fans as their body clocks adjusted, while the Rams stayed home until less than two days before kickoff, keeping their body clocks on California time. Both teams started with understandable sluggishness for a 10:35 a.m. kickoff, but Williams’ TD run finally got the crowd cheering. The quarterbacks then traded interceptions before Purdy shook off a shaky start and found former Rams receiver Robinson on a 39-yard post route. San Francisco surged out of halftime, with Samuel’s 45-yard kickoff return leading to Evans’ TD catch over new Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson. The Rams drove deep into the red zone, but after Puka Nacua was ruled down inches outside the goal line, the 49ers stuffed Stafford.

articles.title: 49ers' De'Zhaun Stribling ruled out of win vs. Rams with left ankle injury
articles.summary: Rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling left with a non-contact injury.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers ' bad injury luck followed them to Australia.

Rookie 49ers receiver De'Zhaun Stribling left Thursday's win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, with a left ankle injury and was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

After the game, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed Stribling's ankle injury but said that his Achilles tendon was intact. The severity of the ankle issue is yet to be determined.

The 49ers have 10 days off before their Week 2 game at home against the Miami Dolphins in Week 2.

Stribling, the 49ers' second-round pick (33rd overall), started the game against the Rams but left with what appeared to be a non-contact injury in the second quarter. After running a route, he came up favoring his left leg and was unable to put any pressure or weight on it as he came off the field.

Stribling then had to be helped into the blue medical tent before being carted back into the locker room.

The Niners were leading the Rams, 10-7 when Stribling left the game and went on to win 27-7 . He was not targeted on any pass attempts.

Stribling had a standout summer after being considered something of a minor reach in the 2026 NFL Draft. He suffered some brief hamstring tightness earlier this summer, but it didn't slow Stribling down as he elevated the Niners' WR depth chart. He caught 11 passes in two preseason games before sitting out the exhibition finale with a shoulder injury.

Stribling was not listed on the 49ers' Week 1 injury report.

articles.title: Sean McVay Takes Blame for Rams' Loss to 49ers, Calls Season-Opening Blowout 'Humbling'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay placed blame on himself for the team's season-opening 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay placed blame on himself for the team's season-opening 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.

"I didn't do nearly a good enough job," McVay told reporters after the game (0:06 mark). "This is a humbling day for us. This will define us only if we allow it to and today was one of those days. I always look inside out, I didn't do a good enough job getting us ready to go. There were some opportunities where maybe the game could've flipped, but they deserve the win. They were ready to go. We'll look at it, we'll see where we can improve and be better moving forward. This is a good, humbling day."

"Sometimes sports can humble you and today was one of those days," he added (0:47 mark). "I make no excuses."

The Rams took an early 7-3 lead, but couldn't keep up with San Francisco's offense as they were held scoreless in the second half of the contest.

Matthew Stafford struggled in Los Angeles' defeat, finishing 15-of-25 for 155 yards and one interception.

Stafford's 61.2 passer rating was worse than all 17 regular-season appearances that he made during his MVP-winning 2025 campaign.

The Rams repeatedly failed to move the chains against the 49ers, as they converted just two of nine opportunities on third down. They also converted just one of three chances on fourth down, which included a turnover on downs at San Francisco's one-yard line in the third quarter.

Los Angeles added reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and star cornerback Trent McDuffie during the offseason, but couldn't slow down the 49ers' offense.

San Francisco racked up 379 total yards, averaging 5.9 yards per play. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy went 25-of-34 for 205 yards and three touchdowns despite getting picked off once.

Meanwhile, Garrett failed to record a tackle or sack in his Rams debut.

McVay will now look to help his team get back on track during a Week 2 matchup with the New York Giants on Sept. 21.

articles.title: Why the NFL Has Built a Global Spectacle, but Not Yet a Global Sport
articles.summary: "The NFL has unquestionably built America’s greatest traveling show. Whether it has built a truly global sport is still a much tougher call." The post Why th...
articles.body:
I have spent much of this week watching Australian coverage of the NFL and scrolling through social media posts as the 49ers and Rams prepare to play the first regular-season game in Australia. The coverage has been entertaining, enthusiastic and occasionally educational. There have been explanations of the rules, breakdowns of the equipment and attempts to introduce American football to a country that already has a sport called football.

The Aussies are excited. Nearly 100,000 people are expected to fill the Melbourne Cricket Ground . Moreover, the NFL has taken over the city. The Jonas Brothers will perform at halftime, and Tourism Australia has built an advertising campaign around the game featuring wildlife conservationist and television personality Robert Irwin. He's the son of the late "Crocodile Hunter" Steve Irwin. In addition, Netflix will distribute the game globally.

It should be a spectacular event. I'm just not convinced it proves football has become a global sport.

This season, the NFL is staging nine regular-season games in seven countries outside the United States. That represents an extraordinary expansion from the occasional London game of the past. The league is no longer simply testing international markets. Moreover, overseas games have become an important part of its schedule, television strategy and marketing machine.

However, more games in more countries don't automatically mean football has developed deep roots in those places.

I have covered NFL games in London, and the experience was fantastic. Iconic Wembley Stadium was packed. The atmosphere was loud, and the crowd included jerseys representing nearly every NFL team. It felt like a combination of a football game, convention and international holiday for fans who had waited years to see the league in person.

There was no question the event worked. Yet, the tricky question was whether the sport worked.

There is a difference between selling out one game and supporting a franchise for an entire season. Bring two NFL teams to London, Melbourne, Madrid or Munich once a year, and fans are going to attend. It is rare and different. In addition, people plan vacations around it and arrive wearing whatever NFL jersey they own. Even when neither team represented on it is playing.

That proves the NFL knows how to create demand for an event, but it doesn't necessarily mean those markets are prepared to support eight or nine home games. Or follow a team through a 5-12 season, or spend three months demanding the offensive coordinator be fired.

Football remains different from basketball, baseball and hockey. Those sports have genuine international foundations. Basketball produces stars from around the world. Baseball has deep cultural roots in Japan, South Korea, Latin America and the Caribbean. Not to mention Hockey has been established for generations in Canada and throughout Europe.

Those sports aren't merely touring internationally. Moreover, they live there.

American football is still overwhelmingly an American game. There is a considerable gap between watching the NFL and building an organic football culture. The equipment is expensive, and the rosters are enormous. Plus, the sport requires specialized coaching and positions.

The NFL recognizes that challenge. Flag football has become an important part of its international strategy and is now being played in more than 500 Australian schools. Its inclusion in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics could provide the NFL with something international games alone cannot. Kids playing a version of football rather than simply watching it on television.

Until then, the league's greatest international strength may be its ability to turn a football game into an entertainment event.

Australia isn't simply getting the 49ers against the Rams. In addition, it is getting concerts, celebrity appearances, tourism campaigns and a week of surrounding content. This isn't just Week 1. It is a miniature Super Bowl with a much longer flight.

That creates an interesting opportunity for the media covering it.

Beat reporters become travel correspondents. Sports anchors explain jet lag, Australian rules football, and the cultural significance of the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Radio shows discuss flight schedules, meat pies and whether arriving early gives the 49ers an advantage over the Rams.

That is the reality of modern sports media. Reporters are no longer simply attending practice, interview players and write a story. In addition, they shoot video, host podcasts, appear on radio, and produce social posts. They bring the audience along for the trip. An international game provides a bottomless supply of material.

Understanding of the Rams' defensive front? Helpful.

Willingness to eat Vegemite on camera while pretending to enjoy it? Mandatory.

I'm not criticizing that coverage. I've been consuming it. The location is a large part of the story because the NFL intentionally made it part of the story. Moreover, that may be the real brilliance of the league's international expansion. A normal regular-season game controls the sports conversation for a day or two. An international game can create content for an entire week.

Multiply that by nine games in seven countries, and the NFL has created a season-long global marketing campaign disguised as a schedule.

Netflix makes Australia an even better example. The NFL isn't simply exporting a football game. It is creating a global television event. Moreover, it's designed to generate highlights, social clips, tourism promotion and coverage from media outlets that normally wouldn't spend much time discussing the 49ers or Rams.

The MCG will look spectacular on television. In addition, the crowd will be loud, the halftime show polished, and everyone involved will declare the NFL's Australian debut an overwhelming success.

We should be careful about what that success means. It will prove Australia can host an NFL game. It will prove American football can attract a massive crowd when presented as a rare international spectacle. Nine games in seven countries will prove the league can repeatedly export that spectacle.

It won't necessarily prove Australia needs an NFL team or that any of these markets are ready to support one for an entire season.

The NFL understands the modern sports-media business better than any league in America. A football game lasts three hours. Moreover, a global content event can dominate an entire week.

The NFL has unquestionably built America's greatest traveling show. Whether it has built a truly global sport is still a much tougher call.

articles.title: Tennessee’s QB Faizon Brandon Fuels Lamar Jackson Hype After Explosive 5-TD Debut
articles.summary: Faizon Brandon could hardly have asked for a better start to his Tennessee career.The true freshman quarterback accounted for five touchdowns in the Voluntee...
articles.body:
Faizon Brandon could hardly have asked for a better start to his Tennessee career.

The true freshman quarterback accounted for five touchdowns in the Volunteers' 56-9 win over Furman, completing 13 of 17 passes for 226 yards and three scores while adding 68 rushing yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Brandon's performance earned him SEC Freshman of the Week honors and immediately added fuel to some lofty preseason praise.

Tennessee edge rusher Jordan Norman compared Brandon's mobility to Baltimore Ravens star Lamar Jackson before the season even began.

"I would say, honestly, it's like trying to tackle Lamar Jackson," Norman said. "Somebody who can run, shake you."

Norman made the comparison after seeing Brandon throughout Tennessee's preseason work, specifically pointing toward the freshman's ability to create problems for defenders with his legs.

That is enormous praise for a quarterback who had not yet taken a college snap at the time.

Faizon Brandon Could Not Have Started Much Better

Comparing any freshman quarterback to Jackson is obviously premature. Jackson is a former Heisman Trophy winner and one of the most accomplished dual-threat quarterbacks in NFL history. Brandon has played exactly one college game, and that game came against Furman. That distinction matters.

Still, if Brandon wanted to give Tennessee fans an immediate reason to believe the hype, he accomplished about as much as possible in his debut. His five total touchdowns tied the Tennessee freshman record, and he did most of his damage before the opener had even reached the fourth quarter.

The athleticism that inspired Norman's Jackson comparison was also visible immediately. Brandon did not simply beat Furman from the pocket. He made plays with his legs and showed why Tennessee believed his dual-threat ability could change the offense. The next test should tell the football world considerably more.

Georgia Tech Will Reveal More About Brandon

Tennessee travels to Bobby Dodd Stadium on Saturday for a 7 p.m. ET matchup with Georgia Tech, Brandon's first road start at the college level. It will also be the Volunteers' first game at Georgia Tech since 1986.

Georgia Tech lost its opener 14-13 to Colorado, but the Yellow Jackets were competitive until the final play and drew a sold-out crowd of 52,113 at Bobby Dodd Stadium.

That environment should provide a much more revealing evaluation of Tennessee's freshman quarterback.

Dominating Furman is one thing. Going into another Power Four program's stadium at night and maintaining the same poise, explosiveness and control is another.

It is far too early to determine whether Brandon deserves anything resembling a Lamar Jackson comparison. One dominant performance against an FCS opponent cannot answer a question that large.

If Brandon produces another impressive performance Saturday in Atlanta , the hype surrounding Tennessee's young quarterback will become much harder to dismiss.

articles.title: No. 4 St. Joseph football shuts down Darien as Jake Rios does it all in convincing victory
articles.summary: St. Joseph has now won three of the last four meetings with Darien after the Blue Wave won six straight from 2014-21.
articles.body:
DARIEN - St. Joseph football coach Joe Della Vecchia smiled a bit when he was asked about senior Jake Rios .

" Bugs Bunny ?" he said of the guy who can seemingly do it all for the Hogs.

Rios was in that cartoon mode once again, and was part of a shutdown defensive performance when No. 4-ranked St. Joseph defeated Darien 28-7 on opening night Thursday.

Rios caught a 41-yard touchdown pass from senior Jack Mooney, one of three long TD throws from the quarterback, consistently stymied Darien's special teams with kickoffs into the end zone, and even put a punt at the 1-yard line, which helped lead to a touchdown four plays later.

"He does a lot," Della Vecchia said. "He's kicking off into the end zone, he was big for field position, he's a great punter. There are a lot of things he does that you don't see in the stat sheet. He's big for us every week."

The game was a battle of FCIAC blue bloods, with the teams combining for 23 playoff appearances , 16 CIAC finals berths and 10 championships in the last 12 seasons. Darien had won six straight in the series from 2014 to 2021, but the Hogs have now won three of the last four meetings, including the last two .

For Darien, the opportunities were there but between some dropped passes and missed chances, the momentum never materialized.

"We left a lot of meat on the bone," Darien coach Andy Grant said. "I chart big plays on the sideline and there were like seven and if we could've swung a few of those, it would've been a different game. The punt return cost us, the hitch-and-go cost us. That's discipline, that's focus or a lack of focus and it's lots of things that are correctable."

The teams were sluggish to start. Neither cracked 100 yards on offense in a first half that included nine punts and a turnover on 12 possessions.

The Wave took the initial lead when quarterback Hugh Dunlap connected with Bruce Hopkins for a 36-yard touchdown following a St. Joseph fumble in the first quarter.

The Hogs answered in the second, driving 85 yards and scoring when Justin Daniels got behind the defense and caught a 32-yard TD pass from Mooney.

A little later in that frame, Rios placed a punt inside the 5-yard line and senior Kyle Wicker kept it in at the 1. The Hogs' defense kept Darien there and when the Wave punted from its own end zone, Michael Charland returned the kick 37 yards for a 14-7 lead.

"I've been practicing my special teams a lot this offseason, practicing my punts and my kicks, so it was great to see it work out," Rios said.

Mooney then threw two TD passes in the third quarter, first to Joey Baskin for 47 yards and then to Rios for 41 yards to ice the game for the Hogs.

Jake Rios, St. Joseph: As is typical, the senior did a bit of everything for St. Joseph, catching four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown, starring in the defensive secondary, and handling kickoffs and punts, even pinning Darien back at its own 1-yard line in the second quarter.

"Our theme all week was let the defense win the game for us. Our goal was to score three touchdowns and then we'd have a good chance to win. On offense, we did enough and we let those guys play." - St. Joseph coach Joe Della Vecchia.

articles.title: NFL international slate includes Melbourne, Rio and Paris. What to know about all 9 games abroad
articles.summary: The NFL will play a record nine games internationally this season and they include three cities hosting for the first time: Melbourne, Australia; Rio de Jane...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — The NFL will play a record nine games internationally this season and they include three cities hosting for the first time: Melbourne, Australia; Rio de Janeiro; and Paris.

Jacksonville and San Francisco both play two games abroad: the Jaguars back-to-back in London; the 49ers in Melbourne and later in Mexico City.

Here's some handy information about the games and locations.

The NFL's first international game of the season might be hard to top attendance-wise. Mike Evans , Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel caught touchdown passes from Brock Purdy , and the San Francisco 49ers routed the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 in the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia. There were 100,021 fans at the Melbourne Cricket Ground for the game, the seventh-largest regular season crowd in NFL history. It was the second-largest international NFL match by attendance, topped only in October 2005 when the 49ers lost 31-14 to the Arizona Cardinals before 103,467 fans at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

The league had never staged a regular-season game so far from home — it's a nearly 16-hour flight from the U.S. West Coast. The NFL West matchup kicked off at 10:35 a.m. local time Friday, Sept. 11, in Melbourne — which was 8:35 p.m. Thursday, Sept. 10 on the U.S. East Coast.

"America's Team" is coming to the famed Maracanã Stadium on Sept. 27. The Dallas Cowboys will play just their second-ever regular-season international game when they face the Baltimore Ravens . In 2014, the Cowboys beat the Jaguars 31-17 at Wembley Stadium.

Rio is hosting for the first time and has what looks like a good QB matchup: Dak Prescott vs. Lamar Jackson . The league has committed to playing at least three regular-season games in Rio over the next five years. There have been two previous games in Brazil — both in Sao Paulo.

Dallas to Rio is an estimated 10-hour flight.

The Maracanã has staged two men's World Cup finals — in 1950 and 2014. It was also the site of the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2016 Summer Olympics.

London has been a mainstay for the NFL since 2007. Forty-two of the 62 regular-season games played internationally so far have been staged in London. Three more are on tap this season.

The first two will be at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium: Indianapolis vs. Washington on Oct. 4; and Philadelphia vs. Jacksonville on Oct. 11.

The Jags pull double duty by staying to face the Houston Texans on Oct. 18 at Wembley Stadium — and by doing so will become the first team to play two home games abroad in the same season . The Jags, who have a 7-7 record in London games, are undergoing stadium renovations at home.

Washington's only other trip to London ended in a 27-27 tie — or a "draw" as the locals would call it — with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2016. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will look to make his international debut after missing last year's Madrid game because of injury.

The NFL finally makes it to the City of Light. Practices in the shadow of the Eiffel Tower perhaps?

The New Orleans Saints have the French connections and the Pittsburgh Steelers have the star quarterback — Aaron Rodgers — for the first regular-season game in Paris. The 42-year-old Rodgers headlined Dublin's debut as a host city last season and figures to be in the spotlight at Stade de France on Oct. 25.

The 80,000-seat stadium, located just north of the capital in Saint-Denis, was the centerpiece of the 2024 Paris Olympics — Tom Cruise descended from the roof during the closing ceremony. It opened in 1998, when it hosted the FIFA World Cup final — France beat Brazil 3-0.

Joe Burrow goes international for the first time — as a player anyway. The Bengals quarterback was a hit at Vogue World 2024 in Paris.

He's set to make his international debut at Bernabeu Stadium when Cincinnati faces the Atlanta Falcons on Nov. 8. It will be Cincinnati's first game outside the U.S. since a 24-10 loss to the Rams in London in 2019 in Zac Taylor's first season as head coach. The Falcons lost to the Colts in Berlin last season.

The 83,186-capacity Bernabeu is home to Real Madrid soccer club — one of the most recognized sporting brands in the world. Real Madrid's soccer team has more Instagram followers — 180 million — than the combined total of all 32 NFL teams.

Last year, Bernabeu hosted Spain's first regular-season game when the Miami Dolphins , led by quarterback Tua Tagovailoa , beat the Washington Commanders 16-13 in overtime . Tagovailoa has since joined the Falcons.

The Patriots-Lions matchup in Bavaria looks promising. New England reached the Super Bowl last season but the big draw will be a homecoming for Detroit wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown . The star's mother was born in Germany and he has a big following among the NFL's large German fan base .

The Nov. 15 game at Bayern Munich's home stadium will be the third NFL game in Munich. The first one, in 2022, was Germany's first regular-season NFL game and Tom Brady led the Tampa Bay Buccaneers past the Seattle Seahawks 21-16. Days earlier, Brady had been gifted lederhosen . The crowd sang 'Take Me Home, Country Roads' — and the seven-time Super Bowl champion called it "one of the great football experiences that I've ever had."

Note to visiting fans, if you enjoy downing pre-game beers, probably best to bring some with you on the train ride to the stadium. Seahawks fans complained no alcohol was served by vendors outside the venue.

The NFL returns to Mexico City for the first time since 2022 for a matchup between the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 22.

Azteca Stadium , which has been renamed Banorte, hosted the very first regular-season game played outside the U.S. when the Arizona Cardinals beat San Francisco 31-14 in 2005 before a crowd of 103,467. (A Cowboys-Giants regular-season game in 2009 eclipsed 105,000). The first play from scrimmage was a wild one — a strip-sack that resulted in a touchdown.

Four years ago, the 49ers were prepared for the high altitude and beat the Cardinals 38-10. Azteca then underwent renovations for the 2026 World Cup and its current capacity is 87,523.

The Vikings played in Dublin and London in consecutive weeks last season and are 5-1 overall in regular-season international games.

articles.title: NFL Insider Reveals Next Step Before Josh Jacobs Decision
articles.summary: Now that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property, the NFL will begin...
articles.body:
Now that Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property, the NFL will begin its investigation and determine its discipline for the three-time Pro Bowler. Jacobs is currently on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

Before the league decides whether to suspend Jacobs and for how long, it would like to interview Jacobs, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.

"In order for the NFL to suspend Josh Jacobs, which, from my understanding, is still possible, they would like to interview him, and they would like to continue to the fact-finding process," said Rapoport.

Rapoport added that while the NFL does investigate further and talk to Jacobs, the time that he misses on the exempt list will add to his suspension time.

"He could, in fact, be taken off the Commissioner's Exempt list and then suspended, and if he does miss games while on the Commissioner's Exempt list, it would count as time served," added Rapoport.

Now that Jacobs has finished the legal side, the next question is when he will meet the NFL. The expectation would be that a suspension would come afterward.

NFL Wants to Interview Josh Jacobs Before Determining Punishment

Jacobs was initially booked on five allegations after an altercation with his domestic partner in May. Those included felony strangulation charges. However, the charges that were formally filed were two misdemeanors, including battery and criminal damage to property.

The Packers running back was convicted on the battery charge and fined $1,000, and the court accepted a deferred judgment agreement on the charge of criminal damage to property. The follow-up court hearing was scheduled for September 10, 2027.

The legal proceedings have concluded, so the NFL will now have more access to information regarding the case.

As the team awaits the punishment, they are moving forward without Jacobs. Offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich noted that the team plans to utilize a running back-by-committee approach for the time being, while they determine the pecking order.

Their top option right now is MarShawn Lloyd . The third-round pick has been with the Packers for three seasons, but has just six career NFL carries. He has a history of injury issues. He also does not have a long history of a heavy workload, going back to college.

The Packers also have Chris Brooks. However, he is entering his third year in the NFL and his fourth year in the NFL and has one game with more than 10 carries in his career.

Lastly, Green Bay traded the Pittsburgh Steelers for Kaleb Johnson . He is a former third-round pick and is only in his second NFL season. Still, he got benched by Mike Tomlin and the Pittsburgh Steelers last year. This year, Mike McCarthy took over the Steelers and gave him even less of a chance.

So, two coaching staffs have already moved on from the young back with promise. When Jacobs comes back, he will likely have a chance to reclaim the spot as the every-down runner.
