articles.title: Myles Garrett Gives Honest Quote After Rough Rams Debut, Talks Knee Injury
articles.summary: Myles Garrett had a concerning debut for the Los Angeles Rams as the star defensive end had no sacks, tackles or pressures.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett had a concerning debut for the Los Angeles Rams as the star defensive end had no sacks, tackles or pressures.

After the 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, he admitted that he isn't 100 percent following knee issues during training camp.

"This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there, and I've got to be better," he told reporters after the game.

Garrett dealt with knee swelling during the Rams' training camp, with head coach Sean McVay calling him "85 percent" in mid-August. McVay also said at the time that the knee issue was "nothing to worry about," but the team was being cautious with him.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last week that Garrett "didn't do much at all throughout camp," but that the Rams were confident about the reigning Defensive Player of the Year heading into Week 1.

"Myles Garrett had a bit of a knee issue, really didn't do much at all throughout camp," Fowler reported on SportsCenter . "They acquired him in June, brought him in. He hasn't been on the field a ton, but they're not really worried. They know he can roll out of bed and get sacks. He's been ramping up slowly but surely, lifting a lot of weights, now he's on the practice field. I'm hearing he should be good as well."

That report from Fowler explains a lot of what fans saw from Garrett on Thursday. He was far from his typical self and was even subbing in and out throughout the game.

The quiet night marked Garrett's first game since 2018 without recording a pressure.

The Rams sent a hefty package to the Cleveland Browns in June for Garrett, and they expected to get the same player who recorded a single-season record of 23 sacks last year.

That version of Garrett is surely on its way, but he clearly wasn't himself on Thursday.

"Get healthy," Garrett said of his goals heading into Week 1.

articles.title: Los Dolphins vuelven a apostar por España
articles.standfirst: Esta semana han tenido lugar los clinics de Flag Football en Madrid organizados por la entidad de Miami
articles.summary: Esta semana han tenido lugar los clinics de Flag Football en Madrid organizados por la entidad de Miami
articles.body: El fútbol americano en España está en auge desde hace tiempo. Y los Miami Dolphins tienen mucha responsabilidad de ello. Fueron uno de los equipos que disputaron el partido de NFL en el Santiago Bernabéu el pasado año. Sin embargo, también hay otra disciplina que tienen como objetivo que crezca en nuestro país, el flag football. Este deporte es una modalidad del fútbol americano en la que se juega sin placajes. Para sustituir el contacto, los defensores deben intentar retirar las cintas o pañuelos que cuelgan de los lados de la cintura de los atacantes. Es tal la magnitud de este deporte, que será uno de los deportes olímpicos en Los Ángeles en 2028. Los Miami Dolphins ya organizaron el año pasado clinics de esta disciplina en España, unas sesiones para enseñar a entrenadores y jóvenes jugadores las habilidades fundamentales y técnicas. Y este septiembre de 2026, han vuelto a realizarlos para provocar que este deporte siga creciendo. Se han realizado en Madrid y Barcelona. Estas sesiones tienen como objetivo crear escuela. Cada localidad tenía dos jornadas, una para formar entrenadores y otra para jugadores. Además, uno de los innovadores proyectos la NFL FLAG School League en España, que se llevará a cabo esta temporada. Los tres equipos de NFL con derechos de marketing en nuestro país, Miami Dolphins, Chicago Bears y Kansas City Chiefs serán los desarrolladores de esta liga estudiantil que contará con colegios de Madrid, Aragón y Cataluña, con otras regiones invitadas a participar. La temporada culminará con el NFL FLAG Spain National Championship en Madrid, en mayo de 2027, donde el equipo ganador obtendrá la clasificación para representar a España en el NFL FLAG World Championships de Indianápolis (EEUU). El 9 de septiembre tuvo lugar en el Estadio Polideportivo Cerro del Telégrafo la sesión dedicada a los entrenadores, a la que acudió MARCA. Al igual que se hace en Estados Unidos, esta sesión de entrenamiento también iba a contar con su parte de ‘show’. La jornada para entrenadores, comenzó con los participantes entrando desde una de las esquinas atravesando un pasillo de miembros organizadores. Con una foto grupal y un grito de apoyo a los Dolphins, tocaba comenzar con el entrenamiento. Asistieron una gran cantidad de personas, tanto hombres como mujeres. Pero el número no fue el único factor diferenciador. Se dividieron en dos grupos, uno para profesores de institutos que aspirasen algún día a dar el paso a los banquillo, y otros que ya son entrenadores en clubes locales. El grupo de ‘más nivel’ contaba con un entrenador profesional. Y en el otro lado del campo, se dividieron a su vez en cuatro subgrupos, cada uno con monitores tanto americanos como españoles, para comenzar desde lo básico para ir poniendo los cimientos. La sesión duró dos horas y media. Los últimos 15 minutos, algunos integrantes de cada grupo pusieron en práctica los conocimientos aprendidos enfrentándose en una pequeña práctica. Una forma de hacer crecer un deporte, que cada año va en aumento.

articles.title: Myles Garrett posts zeros across board in shocking Rams debut in defeat to 49ers
articles.summary: If you’re looking for Myles Garrett’s name in the box score of his Los Angeles Rams debut, you can stop. You’re not going to find it.
articles.body:
If you're looking for Myles Garrett 's name in the box score from his Los Angeles Rams debut, you can stop. You're not going to find it.

Like the rest of his Rams teammates, Garrett posted a dud Thursday night in a 27-7 shellacking at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers . It's a result that will reset expectations in a stacked NFC West and for the Rams in particular as the anointed preseason Super Bowl favorites.

But for Garrett, the effort was particularly jarring. The reigning, two-time Defensive Player of the Year who set the NFL's single season sack record last season failed to make an entry into the box score.

He didn't log a sack. He didn't log a quarterback hit. He didn't log a tackle. He didn't log a tackle assist. He didn't log a past defended. He certainly didn't force a fumble or recover one. It was not what the Rams or their fans were hoping for when they paid a premium price to acquire him from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason.

After the game, Garrett told reporters that he's not 100% from a knee issue that limited him in camp . He also acknowledged the obvious:

"This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there, and I've got to be better," Garrett told reporters, per the Associated Press' Greg Beacham .

This lack of pressure from the Rams defense in part allowed Brock Purdy and San Francisco 's offense to have their way.

The 49ers entered halftime with a 10-7 lead thanks to a 39-yard touchdown connection from Purdy to Demarcus Robinson in which Purdy had all time the time in the world to make the downfield throw.

After halftime, the 49ers blew the game open. They drove 51 yards on seven plays on the opening drive of the third quarter that ended with Purdy's second touchdown of the game. After a goal-line sand by San Francisco's defense, the 49ers marched 99 yards for another touchdown and a 24-7 lead. At that point early in the fourth quarter the game was all but over.

Purdy faced little to no pressure throughout the game and finished the contest without taking a sack. The result was a 25-of-34 passing day for 205 yards with 3 touchdowns and 1 interception.

It was the exact type of effort the Rams acquired Garrett to prevent. On Thursday, like most of the rest of his Rams teammaates, Garrett just didn't have it. He'll leave Melbourne having made literally no statistical impact in his first game as a member of the Los Angeles Rams.

Is it time to panic in Los Angeles? Certainly not. While rare, Garrett has posted these lines before. In fact, it was his fourth career game with zeroes across the board in the box score.

None of those previous three efforts from 2023 and 2024 prevented Garrett from being named first-team All-Pro or tarnished his repuation as arguably the best defender of his generation. And soon enough, he'll share a defensive line with Aaron Donald and do so back in the northern hemisphere.

There are certainly much better days to come for Garrett and likely for the Rams. But the way the Rams lost on Thursday was jarring and will raise questions about their once-presumed Super Bowl viability until they prove otherwise.

Doing so will require Garrett to rediscover his All-Pro form.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers beat Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne as Brock Purdy throws three touchdowns in front of 100,000 fans
articles.summary: The NFL hosted its first-ever regular-season game in Australia as the San Francisco 49ers beat the Los Angeles Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground; Myles Garrett made his debut for the Rams following his blockbuster trade from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason.
articles.body:
Purdy passed for 205 yards and scores to Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel in front of 100,021 fans at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground, the seventh-largest regular season crowd in NFL history.

The Rams had entered the 2026 NFL season widely tipped as Super Bowl frontrunners after their blockbuster trade for Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald from retirement. Instead, it would be Purdy and Kyle Shanahan to deliver a stark reminder of a fiercely competitive NFC West division.

Australia's sporting capital revelled in its first real taste of American football - and in a commanding win by the 49ers, who had already won many Aussies' affection by traveling to Melbourne a week earlier than the Rams, who only landed 28 hours before kickoff on Thursday morning.

Passing: Brock Purdy, 25/34, 205 yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT

Rushing: Christian McCaffrey, 10 carries, 68 yards

Receiving: Demarcus Robinson, 2 catches, 50 yards, 1 TD

Passing: Matthew Stafford, 15/25, 155 yards, 1 INT

Rushing: Blake Corum, 10 carries, 54 yards

Receiving: Puka Nacua, 5 catches, 74 yards

A party atmosphere prevailed even with a Friday morning kickoff necessary to hit the lucrative primetime television audiences in the US. The fans got another memorable chapter in this NFC West rivalry as the 49ers blasted the preseason Super Bowl favourites Rams with superior play on both sides of the ball.

Kyren Williams scored the NFL's first Australian touchdown on a five-yard rush to begin the second quarter, but the Rams were a disaster Down Under. Los Angeles hadn't lost by more than seven points since November 2024.

While Purdy's offense managed enough big plays to win, the San Francisco defense frustrated NFL MVP Matthew Stafford into a 15-of-25 performance for just 155 yards. The Niners held the NFL's best offense last season to one score, even stopping Stafford on a fourth-down quarterback sneak from the San Francisco one in the third quarter.

"They outplayed us in every facet," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "I didn't do nearly a good enough job. This was a humbling day for us. This will only define us if we allow it.

"Sometimes sports can humble you, and today was one of those days. I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it was about travel, whatever, we just weren't good enough in that window."

Garrett was practically a non-factor in his Rams debut after missing much of training camp with aches, recording zero tackles. Donald had not made the trip to Australia as he continues to work his way back into football shape following his decision to come out of retirement.

Much of the pregame talk for this trip centered around the teams' starkly differing methods of preparation: The 49ers ingratiated themselves to the local fans as their body clocks adjusted, while the Rams stayed home until less than two days before kickoff, keeping their body clocks on California time.

Both teams started with understandable sluggishness for a 10:35am kickoff, but Williams' touchdown run finally got the crowd cheering. The quarterbacks then traded interceptions before Purdy shook off a shaky start and found former Rams receiver Robinson on a 39-yard post route.

San Francisco surged out of half-time, with Samuel's 45-yard kickoff return leading to Evans' touchdown catch over new Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson.

The Rams drove deep into the red zone, but after Puka Nacua was ruled down inches outside the goal line, the 49ers stuffed Stafford.

Garrett was critical of his own performance on a disappointing Rams debut that saw him finish tackle-less in Australia.

He acknowledged after the game the knee injury that saw him miss much of training camp was more restrictive than perhaps first thought.

"This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there, and I've got to be better," Garrett said at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

"I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before.

"I wasn't the player that I wanted to be, and I feel like I wasn't the player I've been before when I've stepped onto that field. I've got to do what I can to get back to that."

Garrett was traded to the Rams by the Cleveland Browns in the summer, featuring as part of a defensive revamp that also included the arrival of cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson.

"We knew we were going to face some adversity this season," Garrett said. "It's game one. We've got to find if we are as resilient as we're saying."

articles.title: NFL: San Francisco 49ers shock Los Angeles Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers record dominant 27-7 victory over Super Bowl favourites Los Angeles Rams in front of a crowd of more than 100,000 at Melbourne Cricket Ground.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers recorded a dominant 27-7 victory over Super Bowl favourites Los Angeles Rams in front of a crowd of more than 100,000 at Melbourne Cricket Ground.

It was the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region, and its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.

The 49ers arrived in Melbourne a week before the game, while the Rams opted to spend just over 24 hours in Australia.

Sean McVay's side are Super Bowl favourites after acquiring defensive end Myles Garrett and welcoming one of the NFL's greatest defensive players, Aaron Donald, out of retirement.

"I love when they [the Rams] came out and they were booing. We were out here for a week. We enjoyed the city. I don't think you can fly 16 hours and be ready to play," 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel told Australia's Channel Seven.

The game came to life in the second quarter as Kyren Williams ran in for a touchdown to give the Rams a four-point advantage following an earlier 49ers field goal.

However, the 49ers hit back as Demarcus Robinson grabbed a touchdown before half-time.

The momentum continued as receiver Mike Evans scored, followed by a touchdown from Samuel - and a second field goal sealed the win for the 49ers.

Quarterback Brock Purdy completed 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards, including three touchdown passes.

McVay added: "I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it's about travel, whatever. We just weren't good enough.

"I didn't coach good enough, and we'll look at it and we'll move forward."

articles.title: Led by Brock Purdy's 3-TD night, 49ers remind NFL that Rams, Seahawks are no sure bet
articles.summary: The Niners showed the NFL this week that their talent and coaching staff threaten their fellow division mates and Super Bowl darlings: the Rams and the Seaha...
articles.body:
The hype continued to ratchet through the offseason.

The Los Angeles Rams corralled former Kansas City Chiefs cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson to stem opponents' passing games, then traded edge rusher Jared Verse and a first-, second-, third-round draft pick each to acquire Myles Garrett .

Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, would team up with quarterback Matthew Stafford , the reigning MVP.

This, for a team that lost the NFC championship last season by just four points.

So yes, the Rams held the best odds to win the Super Bowl, at +500, per DraftKings. Next in the NFC West came the reigning Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks , their 11-1 odds fourth in the league.

Continue down the list long enough, and fans would find the San Francisco 49ers ' 19-1 odds. Eleven teams were considered better locks to reach the biggest stage.

Then Thursday happened. Or Friday, at the game's site of Melbourne, Australia.

The San Francisco 49ers, that team so far down the betting list they probably warrant a scroll, beat the Rams in a decisive 27-7 dismantling .

Sure, it's one game in the first week of the season and the first NFL regular-season game in Australia.

But the Rams' cracks are now evident. And the 49ers' quiet but powerful strength should scare the rest of the league.

No matter that 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan missed parts of early training camp due to a car accident that caused a concussion or that reports from the 49ers training camp seemed to float enough injuries to leave electrical substation jokes difficult to ignore.

No matter that the 33rd overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, was carted off the field with an ankle injury in the second quarter .

How about 33-year-old Mike Evans , 31-year-old Demarcus Robinson and 30-year-old Deebo Samuel Sr. scoring the 49ers' trio of touchdowns from quarterback Brock Purdy ?

The Rams' defense that was assembled to instill fear instead instilled confidence in the 49ers as they dominated the time of possession.

"The defense was giving us our ones and twos in the progression," Purdy said after carving up the Rams for 205 yards passing and another 29 yards rushing. "So I was just trying to take that. And then obviously when it wasn't there, I think that was the time of the game where I started using my legs a little bit and the guys did a great job on the scramble drill. ….

"Kyle was doing a great job with dialing up the right play-calls."

The lore of Shanahan exploiting schematic weaknesses from Rams head coach Sean McVay far more often than the rest of the NFL will continue. McVay gave credit where credit was due.

"They outplayed us in every facet," he said postgame. "I didn't do nearly a good enough job. This is a humbling day for us. This will define us only if we allow it to. …

"The first thing I'm gonna look at is myself."

Sean McVay after loss to 49ers: 'Sports can humble you'

Perhaps the 49ers' offense entered this season with some respect.

Shanahan will always cause problems for opponents, and the 49ers have ranked top 10 in offensive yardage each of the last five seasons.

Their core could be knocked for its age — add 32-year-old tight end George Kittle and 38-year-old left tackle Trent Williams to the Pro Bowlers north of 30 on their roster — and questioned for its health track record, which is not unrelated to its age.

But few wondered whether a core with those players, Purdy and Christian McCaffrey could compete if healthy.

Their defense, meanwhile, struggled last year. And it was easy to wonder whether that fall from the eighth-ranked unit in 2024 to the 20th-ranked in 2025 might be a sign of age rather than just a really bad injury streak for players like linebacker Fred Warner and edge rusher Nick Bosa .

Then Warner, Bosa and a group of teammates, including Renardo Green with an interception on Friday, faced the Rams.

The 49ers denied Matthew Stafford a touchdown after he scored one in every single game last season.

The 49ers held the Rams to 7 points, the worst output of Stafford's 85 games as a Ram, regular season and playoffs included.

The second-fewest points Los Angeles had scored in the Stafford era: 9, in 2022. The opponent in that 24-9 loss: the 49ers.

"Sometimes sports can humble you and today was one of those days," McVay said. "I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it's about travel, whatever, we just weren't good enough in that window. …

Against reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, Brock Purdy flashed

The Rams could absolutely rebound as edge rusher Myles Garrett regains health from an apparent knee injury that limited him to zero sacks, tackles or quarterback hits ; defensive tackle Aaron Donald , back from retirement but missing Week 1, should offer reinforcements, too.

But whether or not the Rams settle in, the question will linger: How good can this 49ers team be?

There's reason to believe that the Niners' Australia performance was not a fluke.

Since his 2022 arrival, Purdy has quietly (or not quietly, given the debates that swirl) posted a better passer rating than every active NFL starter but the Baltimore Ravens ' Lamar Jackson . His efficiency and confidence executing Shanahan's anticipatory throwing system continues to grow.

His season-opening performance reflected his range.

Purdy aired out a perfectly timed 39-yard touchdown pass to Demarcus Robinson in the second quarter and nailed the placement on a back-shoulder fade to Mike Evans for a touchdown in the third. When the 49ers' defense stopped the Rams on fourth-and-goal, giving their offense the ball but also a 99-yard field before them, Purdy didn't flinch. He hit a 14-yard pass to get the Niners out of backed-up trouble, later scrambling for 18 yards to pick up a first down and a heaping of momentum.

Facing second-and-8 from the Rams' 15-yard line with 13:04 to play in the fourth quarter, Purdy stayed patient before fleeing the pocket to his right and hit Deebo Samuel Sr. behind two Rams defenders for his third score.

"I thought Brock played so well," Shanahan said. "He had one play I know he wants to take back, the interception of [Quentin] Lake, but he made some big-time plays and big-time throws. The 99-yard drive, there were so many plays there that he had to take off schedule where there wasn't an answer and he moved the chains with his legs …

The Rams, meanwhile, pulled Stafford and starters ahead of their final drive as the double-digit gap loomed insurmountably.

"I think when the ball was kicked off, we were ready to go play," Stafford said. "We just didn't do it at a high enough clip today."

Twenty-eight more teams will play before the week ends, the storylines of the 2026 NFL season only beginning to shape.

But the 49ers reminded the NFL this week that their talent and coaching cast threaten their fellow division mates and Super Bowl darlings: the Rams and the Seahawks.

The team that's advanced to four conference championships and two Super Bowls under Shanahan may need health, but the 49ers otherwise could have the pieces to threaten their deepest run yet.

"Division games, for me, they always count as two," linebacker Fred Warner told "SportsCenter's" Scott Van Pelt postgame. "Regardless of what the headlines say for how people feel about their team or any of the divisional opponents, those division games mean a lot for when we get down to the end. Winning the division, that's always our No. 1 goal: getting to the playoffs, winning our division. So I'm just so happy then that we're 1-0. It was a long week, but it was great. …

articles.title: A quarter century after 9/11, we’ve gone from ‘Never Forget’ to ‘Never Let Them Forget’
articles.summary: We will ask them because that’s what we do. On fields and diamonds from Lewiston, Maine, to Los Angeles, we will ask them. What do you remember? Where were y...
articles.body:
We will ask them because that's what we do. On fields and diamonds from Lewiston, Maine, to Los Angeles, we will ask them.

What do you remember? Where were you when the planes hit the towers? What does Sept. 11 mean to you?

The answers to the questions are changing.

For most of the last 25 years, we have asked athletes to help in remembering the attack on our nation on Sept. 11, 2001. Now we are beginning to ask the generation that can't.

Many of the players participating in the ceremonies weren't around 25 years ago. Those who were born may not be old enough to have the vivid recollections of an older generation.

Nevertheless, they'll stand along sidelines and baselines during moments of silence, wear commemorative patches and listen while names and stories from 2001 are recalled. The NFL will stencil "Never Forget" this weekend in end zones across the country.

The reality is 25 years later, we are transitioning from "Never Forget" to "Never Let Them Forget." We are moving from a time of remembrance to a time of teaching.

My wife and I were driving home from a holiday weekend trip to Washington D.C. recently when we were passing the exit for the Flight 93 National Memorial. We got off the highway on a whim and drove the nearly 20 miles of winding roads through the Laurel Highlands region to visit the crash site.

I wasn't sure what I was expecting, but the scene was overwhelming. The memorial is incredibly well done. It was fairly crowded during our visit perhaps because it was Labor Day and so close to the anniversary. As videos of that day played on a loop in the visitors center and park rangers roamed both inside and outside answering questions about that day, I surveyed the room's demographics and was struck by how many younger visitors had no vivid recall of the events.

Time eventually does this to all of the world's defining moments. Every generation has one, whether it was John F. Kennedy's assassination or the attack on Pearl Harbor. Sports just provide a clear illustration of the evolution.

Tom Brady was a 24-year-old backup quarterback when the planes struck the World Trade Center. He was early into his second NFL season and didn't even take over the starting job until later that month. Now he's retired and carried all those Super Bowl rings with him into the broadcast booth, clearing the way for league MVPs Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen. Both were in kindergarten on 9/11. Brock Purdy and Trevor Lawrence were infants. Caleb Williams and C.J. Stroud weren't even born yet.

Similarly, most current major leaguers were children or weren't born when Mike Piazza slugged that memorable home run at Shea Stadium 10 days after the attacks. Someone has to explain to them why the crowd sounded different, that it was the first sporting event in New York after 9/11 and why Piazza rounding the bases became an enduring image. A regular-season home run in late September is still being discussed a quarter century later. They need to understand why.

That's how this works. We inherit the responsibility of the explanation.

We need to explain that baseball legends like Bob Feller and Ted Williams' career numbers aren't as impressive as they could've been because both men sacrificed three years of their prime to go serve in World War II. Williams later lost two more seasons to the Korean War. Hank Greenberg entered the Army after winning his second MVP and lost three full years and parts of two others to war. All of them American heroes who happened to also be outstanding baseball players.

Legends have their stories stitched into the fabric of the game. Preserving those rich histories is easier than most American institutions because sports is obsessed with lineage. We retire numbers and hang banners and build statues. We rename roads and put names on stadium walls, celebrate anniversaries and invite old teams back to cheer them again.

Now an entire generation of professional athletes has essentially cycled through an entire career since Sept. 11.

For years, asking players about that day produced stories. They remembered practices being canceled or sitting in a college lecture hall watching televisions. They called parents and other loved ones. They remembered the eerie sounds of silence with no planes in the sky and the uncertainty surrounding whether games should be played that weekend. Maybe they couldn't appreciate the gravity of the situation, but certainly grasped the despair we all felt.

Now we have the first generation coming of age with no knowledge and no memories of their own, which perhaps makes ceremonies of remembrance more necessary than ever.

The next generation hearing about Sept. 11 is doing so within a misinformation age that didn't exist 25 years ago. The same phone that shows archival footage from that morning, within a few swipes, offers a theory insisting what they're seeing isn't real or doesn't tell the whole truth.

Social media has made history infinitely more accessible and considerably more dangerous to navigate. Conspiracy theories that once lived on the margins find new audiences through algorithms. Artificial intelligence makes manipulating images, voices and video easier than ever. Distance from events creates a vacuum for alternative versions of the same story.

Within the last couple of years, we've had athletes question if Babe Ruth really existed , insist Michael Jackson is still alive , deny that humans built the Egyptian pyramids and question the existence of space . Just this week, the San Francisco 49ers' Dre Greenlaw wondered if Antarctica is a lie and the Pittsburgh Steelers' DK Metcalf told our Jonathan Jones he believes Antarctica is another world and that there is another civilization inside Earth . Of course, there are a plethora of the standard flat earth and moon landing conspiracies, too.

All of which makes the transition from remembering to teaching about 9/11 so important. Those of us who lived through that day have an obligation to preserve history. We know what we saw. The generation behind us has to decide whom to believe about what happened before they were here. That's why ceremonies still matter.

Sports cannot teach the history of Sept. 11 in 60 seconds before kickoff, but there aren't many settings left that can accomplish something on this scale. A history teacher can only explain the attacks to the 25 students in class and a documentary can only reach those who seek it out and choose to watch. An NFL game has a captive audience of 70,000 people in one building and millions more watching at home. It has the power to interrupt the entertainment long enough to declare that this matters. A moment of silence is an invitation to learn the history.

For 25 years, we asked athletes where they were. Soon there won't be anyone left on the field worth asking. That's when the responsibility shifts to those who were there.

When a player asks what the moment of silence is for, when a child asks why the stadium suddenly stopped moving, it's our turn to answer.

Never Forget was our promise. Never Let Them Forget is what we owe them.

articles.title: Six Key Buffalo Bills Stats Entering Week 1 of the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills officially kick off a highly anticipated season Sunday against the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills officially kick off a highly anticipated season Sunday against the Houston Texans.

With Joe Brady taking over as head coach and fresh faces across the roster and coaching staff, Buffalo enters 2026 with familiar Super Bowl expectations alongside plenty of new questions.

Before Week 1 gets underway, here are half a dozen key stats from the 2025 campaign to contextualize what lies ahead.

What It Represents: The number of 40-yard gains for the Buffalo offense in 2025, which ranked first in the NFL. The Bills scored nine 40-plus-yard touchdowns, while nobody else in the AFC registered more than six scores from that distance.

What It Means: That unit still had some major home-run power, even while becoming more run-oriented than in previous campaigns.

What Has Changed: Joe Brady's offense remains in place with most of the key cogs, following his promotion to head coach, but Pete Carmichael joins as offensive coordinator and quarterback Josh Allen will have a new top receiver in DJ Moore.

What Comes Next: Brady will continue to call plays, so the Bills should expect the status quo to some degree. That said, six of those 16 explosive gains were runs from James Cook (four) and Josh Allen (two), which is phenomenal but less of a guarantee. They may need more deep passing plays. A lot could depend on what they get out of Moore. The 29-year-old has 23 career 40-yard catches but just three since the start of 2024.

What It Represents: Buffalo's record in games against fellow playoff teams that were decided by one score. They beat the Patriots by four in a December thriller but also lost to New England, Houston and Philadelphia by a combined eight points.

What It Means: That, combined with an overtime playoff loss to the Broncos in which they led by four with one minute remaining in regulation, has led to the impression that the team lacked killer instinct toward the end of the Sean McDermott era.

What Has Changed: McDermott is gone. Brady is running the show, while Jim Leonhard takes over a defense that often failed to put games away.

What Comes Next: Leonhard's D is expected to attack more, which is more than half the battle in terms of avoiding complacency. It'll be interesting to see if Brady and Carmichael also adjust their offensive approach after that unit sometimes failed to step on throats in 2025.

What It Represents: James Cook's yards-per-attempt average while the Bills led the league in rushing yardage and touchdowns as the continuation of a philosophical shift in 2025.

What It Means: Buffalo actually scored fewer points than in 2024 but dominated time of possession and had more overall control of games as a result of this approach.

What Has Changed: A strong, experienced offensive line was critical. Cook was by no means a tackle-breaking machine, and in fact, a lot of his damage was done with 3.0 yards per carry before contact (he ranked 13th among qualifiers with a so-so 2.2 yards per carry after contact). But now, with veteran left guard David Edwards gone, he'll be working behind a green starter in Alec Anderson.

What Comes Next: We'll see if Brady and Carmichael stick to that approach, but there's little indication they'll stray. The bigger question is how Anderson will perform with the incumbents around him, and whether we'll see veteran Austin Corbett in there at some point.

What It Represents: The number of rushing attempts (including 33 in the red zone) by Allen in 2025, marking the seventh consecutive season in which the quarterback has registered more than 100 rushes (something only six running backs have done in that span).

What It Means: Allen is a beast who consistently carries this team on his back, as evidenced by his 18 rushing first downs and six touchdown runs in the fourth quarter of one-score games the last two seasons (compared to five first downs and one touchdown under those circumstances from the team's star running back, Cook).

What Has Changed: Allen turned 30 this offseason.

What Comes Next: Ideally, another healthy season for a workhorse who hasn't missed a start since his rookie season but has been exposed to a wild amount of wear and tear this decade. In terms of offensive adjusted games lost , the Bills had the healthiest offense in the NFL last season. They'll need to hope that the injury gods continue to favor them in 2026.

What It Represents: The percentage of Bills red-zone trips that resulted in touchdowns, which ranked third in the NFL (after ranking second in 2024). They were the only offense in the NFL to hit 66 percent in the red zone and register a third-down success rate above 44 percent (44.1).

What It Means: The Bills remain extremely good at extending and finishing drives, which explains why they settled for a league-low 21 field-goal attempts and punted just 3.2 times per game in 2025.

What Has Changed: Really just the addition of Moore and Carmichael.

What Comes Next: Ideally, a lot more of the same. If opposing defenses finally find ways to get this offense off the field, if the offense gets bogged down trying to force-feed Moore, or if the injury bug finally bites, trouble could follow.

What It Represents: The percentage of Bills defensive third downs that resulted in conversions, which ranked in the bottom nine in the NFL for the second year in a row. They also have the league's seventh-worst red-zone defense over the course of the last two seasons.

What It Means: The Bills struggled mightily to get off the field and close out defensive series, which explains why opponents rarely settled for three points—attempting a league-low 50 field goals against Buffalo since the start of 2024

What Comes Next: A new approach with new faces at all three levels of the defense, which the Bills hope will lead to more stops in key moments in 2026.

articles.title: Last-Minute Bold Predictions for the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Throughout the offseason, I've rolled out bold NFL predictions as the league shifted under our feet.
articles.body:
Throughout the offseason, I've rolled out bold NFL predictions as the league shifted under our feet.

Already on the record: Green Bay will finish in the NFC North basement, New England will miss the playoffs entirely, Tampa Bay will fall off a cliff, the Rams will stumble under market expectations, Cleveland will be better than terrible, and Indianapolis will crash and burn.

Now, on the eve of the first Sunday of the 2026 NFL campaign, it's time to empty the notebook with six fresh bold calls regarding the new season.

Volatility is the default setting in the NFC East, where I don't trust anyone in the division. The Eagles deservedly remain the team to beat, but I wouldn't be surprised if significant offensive turnover leads to early inconsistency.

Meanwhile, Dallas and Washington continue to face massive questions about their defenses, at the very least.

I like that the Giants are loaded with young talent on both sides of the ball. I love that they've now combined that with a Super Bowl-winning head coach, a Super Bowl-winning offensive coordinator and veteran additions like Isaiah Likely and Tremaine Edmunds.

I get the feeling Jaxson Dart and his young, high-energy supporting cast will approach 2026 with a nothing-to-lose mentality, which is dangerous if you're Dallas, Philly or Washington.

I'm expecting progress under a new regime from Dart, Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo—as well as in the trenches on both sides of the ball—as the G-Men shock the NFC East in 2026.

For the First Time in 23 Years, the Pittsburgh Steelers Post a Losing Record

I don't remember the last time a core featuring a quarterback acquired just a year ago and a head coach hired just a few months ago felt this stale.

Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy? What are we doing here, Pittsburgh?

The 42-year-old Rodgers hasn't performed at an elite level since 2021, while McCarthy, 62, has just one playoff win since 2017. Rodgers isn't particularly well supported by an average skill-position group and a good-not-great offensive line. While there are some legends on that defense, that unit was thoroughly average overall in 2025. It's fair to wonder what Cameron Heyward and T.J. Watt have left in the tank.

This is a mediocre team destined for a blowup season and likely to be overmatched by the Ravens and Bengals in the AFC North. It's not a good recipe. It's finally time for the Steelers to endure a poor campaign before entering an inevitable rebuild.

Kyler Murray Leads the Minnesota Vikings to the Playoffs

I'll preface this by stating I think the NFC wild-card race is going to be bonkers. I've already got the Giants leaving Philadelphia, Dallas and Washington in the wild-card picture. There are seven playoff-caliber teams fighting for a maximum of five playoff spots in the North and West (everybody but Arizona).

That said, I get the sense that a rejuvenated Kyler Murray will team up with Justin Jefferson, excel behind a superb offensive line, and—buoyed by a talented and experienced defense—push Minnesota back to the playoffs.

This really is a strong all-around team with a high ceiling when the quarterback isn't getting in the way. Kevin O'Connell might be the guy to bring out the best in Murray.

The 49ers can't ever seem to stay healthy. The Rams are overrated and facing ridiculous expectations and pressure in a jacked division. Within said division, the Seahawks could be in for a Super Bowl hangover after losing some key cogs to the vultures.

Within Minnesota's division, Green Bay is facing a tall task without Micah Parsons for an extended stretch. Detroit is coming off a disappointing campaign. The Bears were only a middle-of-the-pack team in terms of DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average) despite winning the North last year.

Few are giving a lot of love to a Vikings squad that went 14-3 two seasons ago. Watch for them to take advantage of that and slip into a wild-card spot while everybody above rips each other to shreds.

It took longer than many expected, but the 26-year-old former No. 1 overall pick has finally found it.

Lawrence took a major step forward with new head coach Liam Coen in his fifth season as a pro—finally finding stability and an offensive mind with a clear plan and path for him.

That's what we saw as he threw for 15 touchdowns and one interception, posting a 113.2 passer rating in his final six games, as the Jaguars finished the 2025 campaign on an eight-game winning streak.

The competition will generally be fiercer this year than it was in that stretch, but I also expect Lawrence and Coen to take another big leap after a full offseason of review and revision.

Nobody's questioning Lawrence's talent. Now, he has the sensei. Does he have the requisite talent surrounding him? The jury's still out, especially if a now-healthy Travis Hunter is more of a corner than a wideout.

The reality is that a lack of oomph elsewhere on offense (including across the line) could work in Lawrence's favor for MVP consideration if he continues to improve under Coen and keeps the Jags in contention anyway.

Aaron Glenn and Shane Steichen Are Toast by Thanksgiving

In Glenn's case, a leash shorter than two years is a tough break, but I just don't see his defense improving enough after ranking 31st in points allowed in his debut season.

Combine that with his vocal backing of Geno Smith—who is destined to struggle as an over-the-hill turnover machine—and it's difficult to envision an increasingly impatient front office waiting for 2027 to pull the plug.

The Jets are going to be buried well before winter arrives, at which point they'll likely put their coach out of his misery and turn their attention to a big pivot in the new year.

As for Steichen, the Colts are a "meh" team trying to pose as a contender fueled by the false belief that Daniel Jones could be the guy after an aberrational hot streak that ended in a decline and a major injury in 2025.

They have a better chance of falling behind the surging Titans than they do of catching up to the Jaguars or Texans in 2026. I doubt it takes long for the front office to realize that and bail on a guy destined for a fourth consecutive non-playoff campaign since taking over in 2023.

A Bills-Lions Super Bowl Finally Comes to Fruition

Finally, a fun Super Bowl prediction that many neutral NFL observers would love to see take place.

Two of the league's most lovable all-time losers. The Lions are the only continuously operating franchise that has been in existence for the entirety of the Super Bowl era without playing in the game, while the Bills are also members of the no-Lombardi club despite having four consecutive kicks at the can a generation ago.

Both teams have been prime contenders for much of the last decade. Now, their windows are arguably closing. I have a feeling it will come together for both of these extremely talented, battle-tested teams as they work under increased pressure in 2026.

Detroit has an easier path than any other NFC heavyweight. You'd have to think better injury luck will be on their side after they led the league by a comical margin in defensive adjusted games lost in 2025. Meanwhile, the Bills have the best quarterback in the world right now, with a fresh feel as Joe Brady takes over the operation and DJ Moore joins the fray as Allen's top weapon.

This is the year. As for who will come through and win it all, I'll wait to make that bold prediction until just ahead of Valentine's Day.

articles.title: Week 1 Waiver Wire Pickups and Advice for Preseason Sleepers Who May Be Available
articles.summary: We're only two games into the 2026 NFL season, which means that fantasy managers still have opportunities to find value on the waiver wire.
articles.body:
We're only two games into the 2026 NFL season, which means that fantasy managers still have opportunities to find value on the waiver wire.

While many managers will wait until after Week 1 to bolster their rosters, they could be wasting a prime opportunity. After all, it's typically easier to snag a player before his breakout game than after. A few players are worth a preemptive flier, especially for managers who have expendable players on the back end of their rosters.

Here, you'll find a look at the top waiver targets who are likely to be available before Sunday's games.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The Miami Dolphins aren't expected to be very good in 2026. They lack proven playmakers on both sides of the ball, and they parted with most of their established stars during the offseason.

Yet, quarterback Malik Willis has an intriguing amount of upside heading into the 2026 season. His supporting cast isn't great, but his dual-threat ability could lead to some massive fantasy outings in most formats.

Willis made just one start for the Green Bay Packers last season, but he racked up 31.5 fantasy points against the Baltimore Ravens. A similar performance against the rebuilding Las Vegas Raiders this week will make Willis a coveted waiver target entering Week 2.

This could put Willis entirely out of play for managers who win their Week 1 matchups. Right now, he's only rostered in 16 percent of fantasy leagues.

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

I'm going to continue pounding the table for speedy Las Vegas Raiders rookie Mike Washington Jr. The Arkansas product is an ideal complement to Ashton Jeanty in Klint Kubiak's offense, and he should see a fairly prominent role in what I expect to be a two-back rotation—not unlike the Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet pairing that Kubiak employed last season.

Washington could see an especially large role in Week 1, as Jeanty makes his way back from a sprained ankle. Jeanty returned to practice on Wednesday, but following a two-week absence, Las Vegas may look to ease him into action.

Right now, Washington is rostered in only 24.3 percent of fantasy leagues. However, that number will skyrocket if he sees double-digit carries and makes the most of them against a suspect Dolphins defense.

The advice here is to scoop up Washington now.

If you followed the Baltimore Ravens at all during training camp and the preseason, you'll know that rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane was arguably the biggest standout of the summer. He's already well positioned to become Baltimore's No. 2 receiver opposite Zay Flowers sooner rather than later.

And there's a very strong chance that Lane has the sort of NFL debut that makes him difficult to land on the Week 2 wire.

For one thing, Flowers has been dealing with a hamstring issue and popped up on Wednesday's i njury report as a limited participant. If he isn't at 100 percent, that could mean extra opportunities for Lane.

Secondly, we don't know exactly what sort of offense to expect from new coordinator Declan Doyle. If Baltimore decides to air it out against the Indianapolis Colts more than they might have in recent seasons, Lane's fantasy stock could take a massive jump.

Heading into Week 1, Lane is only rostered in 9.8 percent of leagues.

My advice to managers who don't already have two star tight ends is to try grabbing Juwan Johnson now. The New Orleans Saints pass-catcher finished last season as TE8 and could be even more productive in 2026.

Quarterback Tyler Shough is entering his second season, and if he makes a jump, so could Johnson's production. With rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson opening the season on injured reserve, Johnson should also have a huge role in the passing game early.

This week, Johnson will face a Detroit Lions defense that has several question marks in the secondary. As Shough's No. 2 target behind Chris Olave, he could have strong numbers against a defense that ranked 20th in passing yards allowed and 26th in passing touchdowns allowed last season.

Johnson is currently rostered in 32.8 percent of leagues, but that percentage will rise significantly if he has a big game in Week 1.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Week 1 Fantasy Football Rankings, Matchups, Box Score Projections for Stars We Love
articles.summary: For fantasy managers, Week 1 is usually filled with twists, turns, and unexpected results. Entering the initial slate, some roles remain unclear, and some teams are still underprepared after limited preseason experience.
articles.body:
For fantasy managers, Week 1 is usually filled with twists, turns, and unexpected results. Entering the initial slate, some roles remain unclear, and some teams are still underprepared after limited preseason experience.

In Wednesday's opener, for example, the Seattle Seahawks were limited when Sam Darnold exited the game with a hip injury, but they were also hampered by a whopping 10 penalties.

A certain amount of guesswork usually goes into Week 1, though managers can at least make educated guesses by leaning into consistent past results, prominent projected roles, and favorable matchups.

Here, you'll find point-per-reception rankings for the rest of the Week 1 schedule, along with box-score projections for the players and matchups we love the most.

Matchup to Love: Joe Burrow vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

While Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow doesn't usually provide the rushing upside of quarterbacks like Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson, he's usually highly productive as a passer. With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both healthy entering Week 1, Burrow should be a very strong starting option.

The visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers struggled to defend the pass a year ago and surrendered the second-most fantasy points (tied) to opposing quarterbacks in 2025. The addition of rookie pass-rusher Rueben Bain Jr. will help some, but Burrow should still have a productive statistical outing.

The Bucs should bring their own potent offense, led by Baker Mayfield, Emeka Egbuka, and Bucky Irving. This should keep Cincinnati passing for much of the game and deliver a solid performance to Burrow's managers.

Box-Score Projection: 395 passing yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 28 rushing yards

Matchup to Love: Omarion Hampton vs. Arizona Cardinals

If he can stay healthy in 2026, Omarion Hampton should experience a big second-year jump. The Los Angeles Chargers starter had several bright performances as a rookie last season but also battled injuries throughout the season.

Hampton should get off to a strong start against an Arizona Cardinals team that wasn't particularly good at defending the run last season. Only the Bengals surrendered more fantasy points to opposing RBs in 2025.

Managers may also see Hampton used in creative ways under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Don't be surprised if he has a notable role in the passing game early before closing out the game on the ground.

Box-Score Projection: 118 rushing yards, 1 TD, 6 receptions, 67 receiving yards

Matchup to Love: Chris Olave at Detroit Lions

There are several reasons to love New Orleans Saints receiver Chris Olave in Week 1. The biggest is that Tyler Shough is likely to funnel the football to Olave early and often.

Olave and tight end Juwan Johnson are the only truly reliable pass-catchers on New Orleans' roster. The Saints used a first-round pick on Jordyn Tyson to give Shough another weapon, but he's opening the season on injured reserve.

Olave could easily see double-digit targets as the Saints try to keep up with the Lions' own explosive offense. And Detroit could struggle to contain him. Only the Dallas Cowboys surrendered more fantasy points to opposing WRs in 2025.

Box-Score Projection: 9 receptions, 135 yards, 1 TD

Matchup to Love: Kyle Pitts at Pittsburgh Steelers

The Atlanta Falcons have some serious questions at quarterback, where Tua Tagovailoa will begin the season as the start. However, managers should still be able to trust tight end Kyle Pitts in a Week 1 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Pittsburgh surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends in 2025.

Pitts should be a high-volume target in Kevin Stefanski's offense this season. Stefanski has traditionally featured his tight ends in the passing game, even when he's had instability at quarterback. Harold Fannin Jr. averaged 4.5 catches and 45.7 yards per game as a Cleveland Browns rookie last season, and Pitts should have a similar floor in 2026.

Box-Score Projection: 6 catches, 78 yards, 1 TD

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs to face player No. 1 of the 'NFL Top 100' in 2026
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs to face player No. 1, Los Angeles Rams defensive lineman Myles Garret, from the 'NFL Top 100' in 2026 | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
The "NFL Top 100 Players" is an annual NFL offseason tradition. There are a few names from the Kansas City Chiefs expected to make the cut, but there are also many opponents featured in this year's rankings. Player No. 1 is a player they are scheduled to face this coming season.

No. 1 is Los Angeles Rams defensive lineman Myles Garrett .

Garrett started all 17 games he played for the Browns in 2025, finishing the season with 23 sacks, breaking the NFL single-season sack record, and 33 tackles for loss, the second-most in NFL history. He was named first-team All-Pro, earned his seventh career Pro Bowl selection, and won Defensive Player of the Year for the 2025 season. Garrett and J. J. articles.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. linked to trade with NFC East team
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers were urged to trade Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys if the team doesn't pull the trigger on an extension.
articles.body:
The clock is ticking on Joey Porter Jr. 's contract talks with the Pittsburgh Steelers , so much so that the talented cornerback has been linked to an NFC East team amid trade speculation.

According to NFL reporter Jourdan Rodrigue, the Steelers should trade Porter to the Dallas Cowboys if they decide against handing out a massive extension.

"If you're not going to pay Joey Porter Jr., you've gotta trade him to the Dallas Cowboys," Rodrigue said via the NFL Daily podcast. "…My stance has been pay Joey Porter Jr. You know, Christian Gonzalez just got paid. I thought there was some eyeballing of seeing where each corner stood financially, and then maybe the contract getting resolved. I think he's one of the best corners in the NFL. I think so, I think he has such as high ceiling."

Rodrigue finished her argument by reiterating that the Steelers should ultimately move on from Porter if they don't plan on extending him. But honestly, that's a disaster waiting to happen.

The Steelers have historically refused to negotiate contracts mid-season, and the two sides are reportedly far apart on a deal just days from the Week 1 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons . It appears that Porter's extension won't get done, but the move to make is franchise-tagging him, followed by re-trying negotiations. A trade shouldn't even be Plan C at this point.

articles.title: Bengals vs. Buccaneers: How to watch, game time, TV info, online stream, odds, and predictions
articles.summary: Everything you need to know to watch the Bengals first game of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
We are finally going to get to see the Cincinnati Bengals back in action as they play host to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to kick off their 2026 season.

After a disappointing 2025 season, in which quarterback Joe Burrow missed significant time and the defense continued to struggle, it will feel good to see this version of the team get its start.

The Bengals were quite busy this offseason. They added quite a bit to the defensive line. You have players like edge rusher Boye Mafe , defensive tackle Jonathan Allen , and nose tackle Dexter Lawrence come in, and they are expected to drastically improve things. Especially Lawrence, who Cincinnati gave up the No. 10 overall pick in the draft to the New York Giants for.

On the other side, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers took a player many Bengals fans probably would have loved to take if the Lawrence trade didn't happen. Rueben Bain Jr. had to be one of the most over-examined prospects in recent years. He dominated at Miami last season, but concerns grew about his arm length.

Which of these overhauled defensive lines can make the game-defining play?

Location: Cincinnati, Ohio at Paycor Stadium

TV Channel: WXIX-TV (Ch. 19) in Cincinnati, WRGT-TV (Ch. 45) in Dayton, and WDKY-TV (Ch. 56) in Lexington.

Broadcasters: Play-by-Play Kevin Kugler, analyst Daryl "Moose" Johnston, and sideline reporter Allison Williams

Online Stream: Fox One (any device, in market), NFL Sunday Ticket (out of market) and NFL Game Pass International (International, excluding China)

Radio Broadcast: Bengals Radio Network: Cincinnati flagship stations WCKY (1530), WEBN-FM (102.7) and WLW700. Click here to view full radio coverage. SiriusXM Ch. 193, Bengals-Buccaneers game center nationwide on desktop , in-market on official Bengals mobile app . Broadcasters are Dan Hoard (play-by-play), Dave Lapham (analyst), and Tony Pike (analyst).

Series Leader: Tampa Bay leads the series, 7-6

Weather: According to NFL Weather , the game will be in the mid-80s with cloudy skies and a chance of thunderstorms

Odds : FanDuel Sportsbook has the Bengals favored by 3.5 points, with an over/under of 50.5 points.

ESPN : eight of 11 experts are taking Cincinnati

CBS Sports : All seven experts are going with the Bengals

Sporting News : Bengals win 34-24 covering the spread

Cincy Jungle: We aren't going to start the season by predicting a loss in Week 1. There is optimism pouring from this team and for good reason. The high-powered offense is intact, and the defense has been peppered with veterans at positions of issue from last year (except linebacker). Maybe that will bite them in the butt, but it feels like we are all sipping the Kool-Aid waiting to bust out the Sexy Dexy dance.

articles.title: Fred Warner Shades Sean McVay Saying Rams Were 'Well Rested' with IG Video After 49ers Win
articles.summary: An 11-month absence did nothing to diminish Fred Warner's ability to dominate, as he showed throughout the San Francisco 49ers' 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night.
articles.body:
An 11-month absence did nothing to diminish Fred Warner's ability to dominate, as he showed throughout the San Francisco 49ers' 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday night.

Following the Niners' impressive performance, Warner threw some shade by posting a clip on his Instagram of Rams head coach Sean McVay's pre-game comment about how "well rested" they were after traveling to Australia two days before the game.

Warner said during his postgame press conference that he felt like the 49ers "got stronger" throughout the game, while the Rams "withered away" as it went on.

Much was made of the different travel plans for the 49ers and Rams with this game taking place in Melbourne. San Francisco arrived last week, while Los Angeles left on Tuesday and didn't land until Thursday.

Based on the results of the game, Warner and the 49ers had the much better approach. The seven points for the Rams were their fewest in a game since Week 9 of the 2023 season against the Green Bay Packers when Brett Rypien was the starting quarterback.

articles.title: Rams' Puka Nacua Addresses 'Darkest Times of My Life,' Rehab Stint During NFL Offseason
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua opened up about the circumstances that led to him checking into a rehab facility during the offseason.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua opened up about the circumstances that led to him checking into a rehab facility during the offseason.

Speaking to Netflix's Elle Duncan before kickoff of Thursday's game between the Rams and San Francisco 49ers (h/t ESPN.com ), Nacua explained he went through the "darkest times I've had in my life" leading up to his rehab stint.

Nacua's attorney, Levi McCathern, told Edward Lewis of the California Post in April that his client checked into a rehab facility in Malibu.

McCathern didn't get into the specifics of Nacua's decision beyond saying the star receiver was working "to improve his overall behavior in every aspect of his life that he can do it."

"I was able to have open and honest conversations," Nacua told Duncan about his time in rehab. "... I'm looking forward most to becoming a person that I think my son will be proud of ... and as my son gets older, I can share some of the things that I've learned from the mistakes I've made."

Even though Nacua has been one of the most productive receivers in the NFL since entering the league in 2023, the Rams did not sign him to a long-term extension in the offseason despite the two sides having discussed a deal. He is currently playing on the final year of his rookie contract.

Nacua started the 2026 season with five catches for 74 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers. He averaged 104 receptions, 1,397 yards and six touchdowns per season from 2023 to '25.

articles.title: Sean McVay Defends Rams' Travel Plan After Blowout Loss to 49ers in NFL Australia Game
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expressed doubt over his team's late arrival in Melbourne being the culprit behind their surprising 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expressed doubt over his team's late arrival in Melbourne being the culprit behind their surprising 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday night.

Speaking to reporters following the Rams' uncharacteristic performance, McVay said, "I don't believe that that's why we didn't play well enough. I really don't. ... I'll always make decisions that I think are best for the football team. It's easy in hindsight to be able to say it was a miss, but those are responsibilities that I'll take."

49ers, Rams Travel Plans VERY Different 👀

The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia pointed out that the Rams' showing on Thursday was worse than any from last season by multiple metrics:

While the 49ers arrived in Melbourne a week ahead of the game, the Rams didn't land until the day before the game, calling into question whether jet lag played a legitimate role in their poor outing.

The Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorite, and they still are, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , at 6-1 odds.

In addition to bringing back a superstar cast that includes the reigning NFL MVP in quarterback Matthews Stafford, wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and running back Kyren Williams, the Rams made a few massive offseason additions as well.

Fresh off breaking the single-season sack record, Myles Garrett was traded to L.A. for Jared Verse and three draft picks.

The Rams also acquired one-time First Team All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie in a trade with the Kansas City Chiefs, plus future Hall of Fame defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of retirement.

Donald didn't play as he continues the ramp-up process after returning to the team, while Garrett was in and out of the game often, coming off knee swelling that impacted him during training camp.

All that is to say the Rams weren't truly at full strength on Thursday, which lends hope to fans of the team that they will improve significantly once they get healthier and more complete.

The Rams will also have the benefit of returning to more familiar surroundings when they host the New York Giants on Monday Night Football in Week 2.

Should the Rams' performance from Week 1 carry over, it might start to become a concern, but a better showing against the Giants would suggest that the loss to the Niners may have only been a blip on the radar.

articles.title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley Wants 'To Say F--k Everybody' over Doubts He Can Have Strong Year at 29
articles.summary: Coming off a down season in 2025, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley has high expectations for himself going into the new year.
articles.body:
Coming off a down season in 2025, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley has high expectations for himself going into the new year.

Speaking to The Athletic's Zach Berman , Barkley said there's part of him that wants "to say f--k everybody" who doesn't think he's capable of having one of the best years of his career entering his age-29 season.

"The competitor in me, who I am to the core, I want to say 'F— everybody. You don't think I'm able to put myself in that category?'" Barkley said. "Why can't I put myself in that category for another five more years? That's the mentality I have."

Barkley's 1,140 rushing yards last season were nearly half of his 2024 output when he became the ninth running back in NFL history to break the 2,000-yard barrier (2,005 yards).

Some of the decline can be attributed to the heavy workload Barkley had in 2024. He had 482 touches between the regular season and playoffs. The single-season record for touches is 492, set by James Wilder in 1984.

Barkley's rushing success rate dropped from 52.5 percent in 2024 to 46.1 in 2025.

A longer offseason, combined with the Eagles changing their offense — Sean Mannion is replacing Kevin Patullo as coordinator — has Barkley feeling rejuvenated as he goes into his ninth NFL season.

"Being a better playmaker," Barkley told ESPN's Tim McManus about his goals for 2026. "That's why I was brought here, that's what I feel I'm one of the best in the league [at] and just bringing that back."

Running back has historically been a younger player's position. Of the 17 players who ran for at least 1,000 yards last year, Derrick Henry and Christian McCaffrey were the only two in their age-29 or older season.

Adrian Peterson in 2015 is the last player to lead the NFL in rushing yards at age 29 or older.

Barkley absolutely belongs in the same category as players like Peterson, Henry and McCaffrey. A new year in a new zone-oriented system could be the thing that gets him back to being one of the elite running backs in the NFL.

The Eagles will be counting on Barkley as they look to make up for some of the production they lost by trading A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots in the offseason.

Barkley and the Eagles will open the 2026 season on Sunday when they host the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field.
